p: פֶּרֶק רִאשׁוֹן (דַּף ב׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "אַשְׁכְּחַן מִשְׁכָּן דְּאִיקְרֵי מִקְדָּשׁ" וְכוּלֵי
Chapter One (page 2a): "We find that the Tabernacle was called a Sanctuary," etc.;
הוּא עִנְיַן "לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא" [וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ], שֶׁכָּתַב בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת חַוַּת יָאִיר סִימָן ר״י שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע פֵּרוּשׁוֹ

this pertains to the mystical principle of acting "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, [and His Shechinah]," concerning which the author of the Responsa Chavat Yair (siman 210) stated that he did not know its inner meaning;
וּבֵאוּרוֹ הַפָּשׁוּט כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין (דַּף ל״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): "אָבִיו" — הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וְ"אִמּוֹ" — כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל

and its straightforward exposition accords with what is taught at the beginning of the chapter Keitzad Mevarchin (Berakhot 35b): "'His father'—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He; and 'his mother'—this refers to the Community of Israel (Knesset Yisrael)";
וְעִנְיַן כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא הָאֵם וּמְקוֹר הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ, אֲשֶׁר מִשָּׁם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת וְלֵידַת כָּל חֶלְקֵי הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for the reality of Knesset Yisrael is the spiritual mother and primal root-source from whence the emanated expansion and birth of all Jewish soul-facets emerge;
וְיָדוּעַ "חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עַמּוֹ", שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם חֵלֶק אֱלֹוקִי
and it is known from the verse "for Hashem's portion is His people" that the souls of Israel are an actual divine component;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו" — מַאן דְּנָפַח, מִתּוֹכוֹ נָפַח
as it is written: "and He breathed into his nostrils," regarding which the Sages established: "He who exhales, exhales from His very core";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְנָתַתִּי מִשְׁכָּנִי בְּתוֹכְכֶם", "אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם הַשּׁוֹכֵן אִתָּם"
and as Scripture states: "And I will set My sanctuary (Mishkani) among you," and "I am Hashem Who dwells among them";
הוּא חֵלֶק אֱלֹוקִי מַמָּשׁ, הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּקֶרֶב כְּלָיוֹת וָלֵב נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
this is an actual divine essence residing within the deepest heart and conscious depths of Jewish souls;
וְהוּא דְּנִקְרָא "שְׁכִינָה" בְּכָל מָקוֹם
and this divine immanence is termed the Shechinah throughout all sacred texts;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְגִלָּה (דַּף כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): "גָּלוּ לְבָבֶל, שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם" וְכוּלֵי
as taught in Tractate Megillah (29a): "When they were exiled to Babylonia, the Shechinah accompanied them," etc.;
וּבְסַנְהֶדְרִין (דַּף מ״ו עַמּוּד א׳): "שְׁכִינָה מַה אוֹמֶרֶת? קַלַּנִי" וְכוּלֵי
and in Tractate Sanhedrin (46a): "What does the Shechinah say [in human suffering]? 'My head is heavy,'" etc.;
לְפִי שֶׁהוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְקִרְבָּם לְעוֹלָם
for She is the revealed Divine Presence dwelling within the children of Israel and inside their very essence eternally;
וּ"מֵעוֹלָם לֹא זָזָה שְׁכִינָה מִכֹּתֶל מַעֲרָבִי" (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ב׳)
and as stated in Shemot Rabbah (2): "The Shechinah has never moved from the Western Wall";
הִיא הַכֹּתֶל שֶׁשָּׁם שְׁקִיעַת הָאוֹר
that wall represents the western horizon where the light sets;
רָצָה לוֹמַר בַּכֹּתֶל שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לַשְּׁקִיעָה, וְהוּא לִפְנוֹת עֶרֶב וְעֵת חֹשֶׁךְ, הַשְּׁכִינָה לֹא זָזָה, מִכֹּתֶל שֶׁהִיא הַמִּשְׁעָן לָאִישׁ
meaning that even when nearing sunset—the twilight hours and seasons of spiritual obscurity—the Shechinah never departs from that protective wall which serves as man's foundational support;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא דַּף נ״ז עַמּוּד א׳): "הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם בְּתוֹךְ טֻמְאֹתָם" גַּם כֵּן
just as it is written in Tractate Yoma (57a): "Who dwells with them even in the midst of their defilements";
כִּי נַפְשׁוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲחוּזִים וּקְשׁוּרִים כִּבְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת, כִּידוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ" (עַיֵּן בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ט׳)
because the souls of all Israel are intertwined and bound together like links of a chain, as is known from the verse: "Jacob is the cord (chevel) of His heritage" (see Bemidbar Rabbah 9);
עַד שֶׁהִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר אֱלֹוקִי בְּהֶעְלֵם וְהֶסְתֵּר וְצִמְצוּם גָּדוֹל אֵין נֶעְלָם מִכָּל לֵב אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל
to the extent that this divine light, though veiled within deep concealment and profound contraction (tzimtzum), is never utterly absent from the heart of any Jew;
אַף הַפָּחוּת שֶׁבַּפְּחוּתִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ חֵלֶק חַיִּים, אֲשֶׁר חָלַק לוֹ הַשֵּׁם מֵחֵלֶק אֱלֹוקִי מִמַּעַל
even the lowliest of individuals harbors an indelible spark of spiritual life allotted to him by Hashem from the Divine inheritance on High.
וְנִקְרֵאת בְּכָל מָקוֹם הַשְּׁכִינָה בִּלְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה, כִּי הִיא בְּמַדְרֵגַת אֵם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
The Shechinah is consistently referenced in the feminine form because She exists at the maternal level, as mentioned above;
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת עֶצֶם אוֹר הַשֵּׁם גָּדוֹל מְאֹד, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת מֻשָּׂג לְלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם כְּלָל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וָחָי"
this is because the essential transcendent Light of Hashem is infinitely beyond grasp and cannot be directly perceived by the mortal human heart, as written: "For no man shall see Me and live";
וְזֶהוּ תֹּאַר "הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא" — הוֹרָאַת קְדֻשָּׁה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הַבְדָּלָה, שֶׁהוּא נִבְדָּל מִבְּנֵי אָדָם, וְהַיְנוּ אוֹר הַשֵּׁם הַנִּבְדָּל מִלִּבּוֹת הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי

and this defines the title HaKadosh Baruch Hu (the Holy One, Blessed be He), for holiness (kedushah) always denotes distinction and separateness, signifying that He transcends created humanity as the transcendent Divine Light elevated above direct human contemplation;
וּלְפִי שֶׁרָצָה יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ הַנִּבְרָאִים גַּם כֵּן מֵאוֹרוֹ, צִמְצֵם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶאָרָתוֹ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה מֻגְבֶּלֶת וּמְצֻמְצֶמֶת וְלֹא בְּתֹקֶף וָחֹזֶק כָּל כָּךְ
yet because He willed that created beings should nevertheless receive of His illumination, He contracted His radiance to be channeled and defined rather than intensely overwhelming;

[וְהַתְּשִׁישׁוּת כֹּחַ נִרְמָז בְּכָל מָקוֹם בִּלְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת טַעַם בְּכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "יָכֹלְתָּ, 'יָכֹלְתְּ' מִבָּעֵי לֵיהּ — תָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחוֹ כִּנְקֵבָה" וְכוּלֵי]

(and this intentional softening and containment of force is hinted at through feminine terminology, as our Sages explained in Berakhot 32a: "You said yakholta; it should have said yakholt—implying power held in reserve like a female," etc.);
וְהוּא כֹּחַ אוֹר שְׁכִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹךְ לִבְּבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
and this channeled potency constitutes the manifest presence of His Shechinah within the hearts of the Children of Israel;

וּכְעִנְיַן הָאֵם הַמְּגַדֶּלֶת בְּנָהּ, כָּךְ גִּדּוּל הַחַיִּים הַנִּצְחִיִּים שֶׁבְּנַפְשׁוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא אוֹר הַשּׁוֹכֵן בָּם, וְעַל יָדָהּ מִתְנַהֲגִים כָּל עִנְיְנֵי הַחַיִּים הָאֲמִתִּיִּים וְהֶבְדֵּלָם מִן הַבְּהֵמוֹת

and just as a mother nurtures her child, so too does the nourishment of eternal life in Jewish souls stem from this indwelling light, through which all true, purposeful living is directed, elevating humanity above the beasts;
אֲבָל עִקָּר וְשֹׁרֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר מִמֶּנּוּ הֻשְׁתְּלוּ בְּהֶעְלֵם
but the primary source and root from which these souls were invisibly implanted;
[כִּי הַהַשְׁתָּלָה הַגְּלוּיָה מִן הָאֵם הַמּוֹלֶדֶת, אֲבָל בְּהֶעְלֵם בָּאָה הַהַשְׁתָּלָה מִן הָאָב שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ, וְ"לֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה"]

(for visible nurture comes through the mother who births, but the hidden seminal origin originates with the father, received by her such that "it is not outwardly perceptible that it entered her innermost self");
הוּא מִן עֶצֶם הָאוֹר הַנִּבְדָּל, שֶׁהוּא הַמּוֹלִיד כָּל חֵלֶק וָחֵלֶק אֱלֹוקִי בְּכֹחַ, וְנוֹתְנָם לַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם
derives from the transcendent Essential Light itself, which conceives every divine soul-spark in potentiality and transmits them to the Shechinah, the faculty of contraction;

רָצָה לוֹמַר הַכֹּחַ שֶׁיִּסֵּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיְּצֻמְצַם, וְיוּכַל לָצֵאת לַפּוֹעַל נִרְגָּשׁ אוֹר הַשָּׂגָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֵב בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ הַשְּׁכִינָה הוּא הַמּוֹלִיד וּמוֹצִיא לַפּוֹעַל
meaning the capacity established by Hashem that allows His light to be focused and felt within human hearts, with that very power of the Shechinah actualizing and bringing it to full birth;
וְזֶה פֵּרוּשׁ "אָבִיו" — זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and this is the mystical meaning of the statement: "'His father'—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He."
וְהִנֵּה כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת הוּא עַל יְדֵי חֵלֶק חַיִּים הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹכֵנוּ
Behold, the entire performance of the commandments is carried out through the vital spark of spiritual life dwelling within us;
אָנוּ עוֹבְדִים לְמֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, הַנִּבְדָּל מִכָּל גֶּשֶׁם וְחוֹפֵף עָלֵינוּ
[whereby] we serve the King of Glory and the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who is utterly distinct and elevated above all corporeality yet hovers closely over us.
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵמוּת הוּא הוֹסָפוֹת הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרִבּוּי יוֹתֵר מוּרְגָּשׁ
That is to say, the ultimate purpose of wholeness and perfection is the increased manifestation of the light of Hashem, Blessed be He, experienced with ever greater tangible clarity,
עַד כִּי "כָּל עַצְמוֹתַי תֹּאמַרְנָה: הַשֵּׁם, מִי כָמוֹךָ"
until "all my bones declare: 'Hashem, who is like You!'".
וְעַל זֶה צִוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חֻקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים, אֲשֶׁר כְּפִי סִדְרֵי הַחָכְמָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
For this very purpose Hashem, Blessed be He, commanded statutes and ordinances, which, according to the structured pathways of Supernal Wisdom,
עַל יָדָם יִזְדַּכְּכוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת וְהַלְּבָבוֹת וְיוּסְרוּ הַמַּסָכִים הַמַּבְדִּילִים
purify souls and hearts through their practice, dismantling the separating veils
עַד שֶׁיּוּרְגַּשׁ יוֹתֵר וְיִתְרַבֶּה הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹוקִי מִמַּעַל שֶׁבְּקִרְבּוֹ
so that the transcendent divine portion within a person is felt more palpably and intensified.
וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּוָּלֵד בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ עוֹד חֵלֶק אוֹר וְהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל עֲבוֹדָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
This means that in the midst of the heart there is born an additional measure of light and divine perception through each and every act of service;
וְכָל לֵידָה הִיא עַל יְדֵי אָב וָאֵם
and since every birth requires both a father and a mother,
הַיְנוּ שֶׁיֻּשְׁפַּע מֵאוֹר כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ עוֹד אוֹר נוֹסָף בָּאוֹר הַמְּצֻמְצָם בְּקֶרֶב הַשָּׂגַת לִבּוֹ

it follows that from the transcendent light of His Glory, blessed be His Name [the Father principle], an additional influx of illumination is channeled into the contracted light residing within the heart's inner perception [the Mother/Shechinah principle],
לְהַשִּׂיג יוֹתֵר מֵאֲמִתּוּת אוֹר וְשֶׁפַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל פְּנֵי תֵּבֵל
enabling one to grasp more of the reality of the light and abundance of Hashem, Blessed be He, across the universe;
[שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית אוֹר הַמְּצֻמְצָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (קִדּוּשִׁין דַּף ל״א עַמּוּד א׳): "שֶׁהוּא וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּבִין בִּכְבוֹד אָבִיו"]
(for this is the very culmination and purpose of the contracted light, as stated in Kiddushin 31a: "both he and his mother are obligated in the honor of his father").
וְעַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת, שֶׁעוֹבֵד בְּכֹחַ חִיּוּתוֹ וְשִׂכְלוֹ הַמּוּשָׂג לְלִבּוֹ וּמוֹחוֹ הַמְּצֻמְצָמִים
And through the practical performance of the mitzvot, wherein one serves with the vitality and intellectual grasp available to one's delimited heart and contracted mind,
עוֹבֵד לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם, אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים וּמֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם
serving the Life of all worlds, the Living God and Sovereign of Eternity,
הֲרֵי מִתְאַחֵד וּמִתְחַבֵּר חֵלֶק הַחַיִּים הַשּׁוֹכֵן בּוֹ לִמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים
the inner spark of life dwelling within him unites and binds directly with the Primal Source of Life.
וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְאַחֲדוּת זוֹ הִיא הַלֵּידָה הַחֲדָשָׁה בְּהַשָּׂגָה נוֹסֶפֶת
Through this spiritual unification, a new birth is brought forth into being, yielding expanded consciousness and higher perception;
וְזֶהוּ פֵּרוּשׁ "לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא" [וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ]
and this is the true meaning of the proclamation "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, [and His Shechinah]."
וְעִנְיַן "בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ, וּרְחִימוּ וּדְחִילוּ"
And the concept of serving Hashem "in awe and love, and in love and awe,"
הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּךָ", וְנֶאֱמַר: "אִישׁ אִמּוֹ וְאָבִיו תִּירָאוּ"

corresponds to Scripture stating, "Honor your father and your mother" [prioritizing the father in honor/love], and likewise stating, "Every person shall revere his mother and his father" [prioritizing the mother in awe/fear];
וְדִקְדּוּק רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (שָׁם) יָדוּעַ
and the precise textual deduction made by our Sages of blessed memory in Tractate Kiddushin (30b–31a) regarding this inversion is well known.
אֲבָל הָעִנְיָן יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּקּוּנִים (תִּקּוּן יוּ״ד): דְּאַבָּא וְאִמָּא הֵם תְּרֵין גַּדְפִין, וְאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּלֹא דְּחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ לָא פָּרְחַת לְעֵילָּא

However, the esoteric meaning is illuminated by what is written in the Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 10): that "Father" (Abba) and "Mother" (Imma) are two wings, and Torah study without awe and love cannot soar upward.
פֵּרוּשׁ הַפְּרִיחָה הִיא שֶׁתְּקֻבַּל בְּרָצוֹן לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
The meaning of "soaring" is that the mitzvah or Torah is favorably accepted before Him, Blessed be He,
עַד שֶׁיִּוָּלֵד תֵּכֶף בְּקִרְבּוֹ שֶׁפַע הַשָּׂגָה מְחֻדֶּשֶׁת
to the point where there is immediately birthed within the person an influx of renewed divine comprehension;
וְזֶהוּ רַק עַל יְדֵי הַהִתְאַחֲדוּת דְּאַבָּא וְאִמָּא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
and this occurs solely through the spiritual unification of Father and Mother, as mentioned above.
וְהִנֵּה דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה גּוֹלֶמֶת בְּלֹא לֵב כַּמּוּבָן
Now, this spiritual ascent cannot be achieved through mechanical, mindless action devoid of heart, as is self-evident,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַחַיִּים שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ וּמִתְבּוֹנֵן בַּחַיִּים הַשּׁוֹכְנִים בְּקִרְבּוֹ
but only through the heartfelt sensation of vitality, wherein one feels and contemplates the Divine Life dwelling within one's innermost being;
וּמִתְבּוֹנֵן בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים הַמְּמַלֵּא כָּל עָלְמִין וְסוֹבֵב כָּל עָלְמִין, אֲשֶׁר לוֹ תִּכְרַע כָּל בֶּרֶךְ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת

and contemplates the ultimate Source of Life Who fills all worlds (Memaleh Kol Almin) and encompasses all worlds (Sovev Kol Almin), before Whom every knee bends in the fulfillment of the commandments.
וְהַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת כִּי "אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם הַשֹּׁכֵן אִתָּם" מוֹלֶדֶת הַיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּהַגָּהָה דְּרֵישׁ אֹרַח חַיִּים, יְעֻיַּן שָׁם

Furthermore, meditating on the reality that "I am Hashem Who dwells among them" engenders awe (yirah), as noted in the gloss of the Rema at the beginning of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim (1:1), see there;
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְיִרְאָה אֶת הַשֵּׁם, הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵין הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת
and as long as a person has not attained genuine awe of Hashem, it is because authentic emotional feeling has not yet permeated the heart.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת בִּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּבְדָּל מֵהַשָּׂגַת שִׂכְלֵנוּ, מוֹלִיד תְּשׁוּקָה וְכֹסֶף עָצוּם לְהַגִּיעַ עָדָיו וּלְהַשִּׂיג אוֹרוֹ הַנֶּעְלָם

And through contemplating the holiness of Hashem, Blessed be He, Who is utterly transcendent beyond human intellectual grasp, there is birthed an intense longing and yearning to reach Him and perceive His concealed Light,
כְּעִנְיַן "נִכְסְפָה וְגַם כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי" וְכוּלֵי, וְהוּא תֹּקֶף הָאַהֲבָה
evocative of the verse "my soul yearns and faints [for the courts of Hashem]," which constitutes the overpowering intensity of love (ahavah).
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיָן שֶׁבְּמוֹרָא הִקְדִּים הָאֵם, וּבְכָבוֹד הָאָב

And this explains why, regarding awe/reverence, Scripture prioritized the mother [the Shechinah/internal immanence where awe begins], whereas regarding honor/love, it prioritized the father [the transcendent Light toward which love yearns];
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ לְכַוֵּן זֶה בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּקִדּוּשִׁין
and this is not the place to elaborate extensively on harmonizing this with the explicit words of our Sages of blessed memory in Tractate Kiddushin.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת, אָז הַמַּעֲשֶׂה פָּרְחָה לְעֵילָּא, וְנִתּוֹסַף לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה וְרִבּוּי אוֹר

When the performance of a mitzvah is grounded in genuine inner feeling of the heart, the deed soars on high, and the individual receives an addition of spiritual comprehension and an abundance of divine illumination;
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה — מִצְוָה"
and this is the inner meaning of what is taught: "The reward of a mitzvah is the mitzvah itself."
[וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה "זָכָה", וּ"זְכוּת" — לְשׁוֹן זַךְ]
[And this is the root of our Sages' phrase zacha (merited), where zechut (merit) is fundamentally an expression of zach (clarified, pure, and refined).]
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן יִחוּד הַמְּפֻרְסָם בְּסִפְרֵי הַמְּקֻבָּלִים, שִׁלּוּב הַשֵּׁמוֹת שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה וְאַדְנוּת
And this is the inner meaning of the renowned unification found in the writings of the Kabbalists: the interweaving (shiluv) of the Names Havayah (the Tetragrammaton) and Adnut (Lordship).
וְאֵין הַכַּוָּנָה שֶׁל הַמְּחַבֵּר בְּשִׁלּוּב הָאוֹתִיּוֹת הַנִּרְאִים לְעֵין הַבְּשָׂרִי
The intended aim of the author is not merely the mechanical interweaving of the physical letters perceptible to mortal, corporeal sight,
רַק בְּעַיִן הַשִּׂכְלִי וְהִתְיַחֲדוּתָם בַּלֵּב כְּפִי הוֹרָאַת רְמִיזָתָם וְהַמְּכֻוָּן בָּהֶם
but rather through contemplative intellect and their profound unification within the heart, according to what their allusions signify and what is truly aimed at through them.
כִּי שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה מוֹרֶה עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּמֶּה שֶׁהוּא בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתֵנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ גְּבוּל
For the Name Havayah denotes the Holy One, Blessed be He, in His infinite expansion far above our finite human comprehension;
כְּמוֹ כֵן שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה מוֹרֶה "הָיָה, הֹוֶה, וְיִהְיֶה", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטּוּר אֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן ה׳
likewise, the Name Havayah denotes "He was, He is, and He will be," as codified in the Tur, Orach Chaim (siman 5),
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין קֵץ הַנֶּעְלָם מֵאִתָּנוּ
which embodies an endless, eternal expansion concealed from our temporal perception,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּפְסָחִים (דַּף נ׳ עַמּוּד א׳): "זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם" וְכוּלֵי, דִּבְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא נִקְרָא בּוֹ, שֶׁאֵין מוּשָׂג כְּלָל

as taught in Tractate Pesachim (50a): "'This is My Name forever (l'olam / l'alem — to be hidden),' etc.," meaning that in this world it is not pronounced as written, because its transcendent reality cannot be grasped at all.
וְאַדְנוּת מוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא אֲדוֹן הַכֹּל וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה
The Name Adnut, by contrast, signifies that He is Master of all and that His sovereignty reigns over all existence;

שֶׁמִּדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת, אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁבִילָהּ הָיָה הַבְּרִיאָה הַגְּבוּלִית וּמְצֻמְצֶמֶת כְּאִלּוּ יֵשׁ נִבְדָּלִין לְגַלּוֹת מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ, שֶׁאֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם (עַיֵּן פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק י׳)

for the attribute of Kingship (Malchut) is the purpose for which bounded, contracted creation was brought forth—appearing outwardly as distinct, separate entities in order to reveal His kingship, "since there is no king without a nation" (see Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 10);
מִדָּה זוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה בְּכָל חֶלְקֵי הַחַיִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, הִיא הַנּוֹתֶנֶת חַיִּים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
this attribute rules over all, bestowing life and vitality to every living facet across the face of the earth, as explained above.
וְזֶהוּ הוֹרָאַת שֵׁם הָאַדְנוּת: הַכֹּחַ שֶׁל אַדְנוּת, וְהוּא הַכֹּחַ שֶׁל הַהִצְטַמְצְמוּת וְהִמָּצֵא בַּעֲלֵי גְּבוּל

And this is the essential designation of the Name Adnut: the power of mastership, which functions as the divine potency of self-contraction (tzimtzum) and the calling into existence of bounded, finite creatures.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב עַל שֵׁם הַהַוָּיָ״ה שֵׁם הָאַדְנוּת
This is the mystery of why the Name Adnut is read and layered over the written letters of Havayah.
וְהַמְּקֻבָּלִים רָמְזוּ עַל פָּסוּק: "וַהַשֵּׁם בְּהֵיכַל קָדְשׁוֹ הַס" וְכוּלֵי
The Kabbalists noted the esoteric allusion in the verse: "And Hashem is in His Holy Sanctuary (Heikhal), let all [the earth] keep silence (has)," etc.,
"הֵיכָ״ל" וְ"הַ״ס" בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "אַדְנָי", שֶׁהוּא הֵיכָל לְשֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה
where the numerical value of Heikhal (65) and has (65) equals the numerical value of Adnay (65), signifying that Adnut serves as the protective Sanctuary (Heikhal) housing the Name Havayah.
רָצָה לוֹמַר: כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ מֻצְנָע בְּהֵיכָלוֹ, וְאֵין עֶצֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ נִגְלֶה רַק הַהֵיכָל אֲשֶׁר מֻצְנָע בּוֹ
This means: just as an earthly monarch remains concealed inside his palace, such that the person of the king is not directly seen but only the palace wherein he is secluded,
כָּךְ הִתְגַּלּוּת שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הָאַדְנוּת שֶׁהוּא מֻצְנָע בּוֹ
so too the revelation of Havayah occurs exclusively through the power of Adnut, within which it is hidden and enclothed.
כִּי חֵלֶק הַחַיִּים אֲשֶׁר נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ הוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר אוֹתָנוּ וּמֵעִיד עַל כֹּחַ שֵׁם הַהַוָּיָ״ה וְהַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד אֵין קֵץ
For the spark of divine life that He planted within us is precisely what awakens us and bears witness to the transcendent power of Havayah and its boundless, endless expansion;
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ
and this is not the place to elaborate further.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל" וּ"בָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד"
And this is the inner meaning of the proclamation Shema Yisrael and the response Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto L'olam Va'ed:
שֶׁ"שְׁמַע" הוּא יִחוּד שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה
for the verse of Shema embodies the unification of the transcendent Name Havayah (Higher Unity / Yichuda Ila'ah),
וּ"בָרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד" מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת וְאַדְנוּת
while "Blessed be the Name of His glorious Kingdom forever and ever" corresponds to the attribute of Kingship (Malchut) and the divine Name of Lordship (Adnut) (Lower Unity / Yichuda Tata'ah).
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַוָּיָ״ה אֶחָד בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר גַּם עַכְשָׁו
That is to say, in absolute truth Havayah is One in total, unbroken unity even now,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, וְאַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם"
as we declare: "You were He before the world was created, and You are He after the world was created";
שֶׁאֵין הַבְּרִיּוֹת חוֹצְצִים כְּלוּם בַּאֲמִתּוּת יִחוּדוֹ
for created beings do not constitute any barrier whatsoever against the absolute reality of His Oneness,
וְאֵין חֶלְקֵי הַחַיִּים הַנִּגְלִים בָּעוֹלָם מְצֻמְצָמִים וּמוּגְבָּלִים נִפְרָדִים מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים הַנִּצְחִיִּים וּבִלְתִּי בַּעַל גְּבוּל
and the facets of life revealed within this world, contracted and bounded though they appear, are not truly severed from the eternal, boundless Source of Life.
רַק לְפִי כֹּחַ הַמְּקַבְּלִים, שֶׁאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לְקַבֵּל כְּפִי תֹּקֶף הַהַשָּׂגָה
Rather, it is solely according to the capacity of the recipients, who cannot receive or endure the overwhelming intensity of His direct light;
וְרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִהְיוֹת מֶלֶךְ בְּעָם, וְיִהְיוּ מְקַבְּלִים וּמַשְׁפִּיעִים
and Hashem, Blessed be He, willed to reign as King over a people, establishing vessels that receive and forces that bestow;
וּכְפִי מְעַט שִׂכְלָם יַשִּׂיגוּ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי הַהִצְטַמְצְמוּת
and that according to their modest intellect, creatures might also perceive Him through this process of divine self-contraction (tzimtzum);
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל אַחְדוּת גָּמוּר
yet in ultimate truth, everything remains complete and total Oneness.
וְתַכְלִית כָּל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת לַהַוָּיָ״ה
The ultimate objective of all divine service is directed toward Havayah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף ק״י עַמּוּד א׳) עַל פָּסוּק: "זֹבֵחַ לָאֱלֹהִים יָחֳרָם, בִּלְתִּי לַהשֵּׁם לְבַדּוֹ"
as the Zohar (Vol. III, 110a) elucidates on the verse: "He who sacrifices to other gods shall be utterly destroyed, save unto Hashem alone";
הַיְנוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַתַּכְלִית שֶׁרָצָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעוֹלָמוֹ, לְפַרְסֵם אֱלֹוקוּתוֹ וְהַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד
meaning that this is the overarching goal which Hashem willed in His universe: to publicize His Divinity and establish the universal recognition that He is One;
וְשֶׁיְּבֹרַר אֵצֶל כָּל נִבְרָא כֹּחַ הַבּוֹרֵא שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה, כֹּחַ הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת עַד בְּלִי תַּכְלִית
and that it become clarified to every created being that the primal power of the Creator is Havayah—the force of endless, boundless expansion;
[שֶׁהוּא] בּוֹרֵא, הַבּוֹרֵא לַנִּבְרָא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וְתַכְלִית
Who creates, the Creator forming a creation endowed with boundaries and finitude,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁלִּזְמַנּוֹ וּמִדַּת יָמָיו גְּבוּל וְתַכְלִית, וְהוּא כֹּחַ מְצֻמְצָם וּמוּגְבָּל
just as man's lifespan and allotted days possess defined limits and an end, being characterized by contracted and bounded power.
וְזֶהוּ צִוּוּי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּכָל בֹּקֶר וָעֶרֶב
And this is the profound purpose of the commandment to recite the Shema every morning and evening:
שֶׁבְּכָל הַתְחָלַת גְּבוּל נִפְרָד מֵהַגְּבוּלִים שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַעֲלֵי הַגְּבוּל
that at the commencement of each distinct cycle of boundaries created by Hashem for finite beings [day and night],
נָעִיד וְנַכִּיר כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַוָּיָ״ה אֶחָד
we bear witness and acknowledge that in absolute reality, Havayah is One;
שֶׁהוּא [הָאוֹר] הַבִּלְתִּי בַּעַל גְּבוּל, וְהוּא מְיֻחָד בְּתַכְלִית הַיִּחוּד שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם פֵּרוּד חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
that He is the infinite, boundless Essence, unified in the ultimate Oneness wherein there is no separation whatsoever, God forbid;
רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא נִרְאֶה שֶׁהַנִּבְרָא הוּא כְּנִפְרָד מִן הַבּוֹרֵא, הוּא כִּי "בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד", כְּדֵי לְגַלּוֹת כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

and that the apparent reality wherein creation seems distinct from the Creator exists solely because "Blessed be the Name of His glorious Kingdom forever and ever"—in order to reveal the honor of His Sovereignty, as explained above.
אֲבָל תַּכְלִית הָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁיַּכִּיר הַנִּבְרָא אֶת הַבּוֹרֵא, הַיְנוּ יִחוּד שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה בְּאַדְנוּת
But the ultimate summit of spiritual service is that the created being recognize the Creator, which constitutes the unification of Havayah with Adnut:
שֶׁגַּם אַחַר שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, הַוָּיָ״ה אֶחָד
that even subsequent to the creation of the physical universe, Havayah is One;
וְהֵם מְיֻחָדִים בְּתַכְלִית הָאֶחָד, שֶׁאֵין חוֹצְצִים כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים בִּפְנֵי הַיִּחוּד הָאֲמִתִּי כַּנּוֹדָע
and these aspects are bound in supreme singularity, such that no created beings constitute a barrier before this true Divine Unity, as is known.
וְזֶהוּ שִׁלּוּב הָאוֹתִיּוֹת, רוֹמֵז שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד בְּכָל חֶלְקֵיהֶם, וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִרְגָּשׁ כָּךְ בַּלֵּב

And the Kabbalistic interweaving (shiluv) of the letters of these two Names alludes to their mutual interpenetration throughout all their facets, meaning that this reality must be palpably experienced within the human heart.
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וְאָז אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה מִתְאַחֲדִים כְּאֶחָד [כְּעִנְיַן "אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק"]

And this realization is attained through love and awe, as explained above, whereupon love and awe fuse into one (in the manner of "Abraham begot Isaac," where lovingkindness gives birth to reverent restraint);
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתָנָא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג׳): "אֲנִי יָרֵאתִי", שֶׁהָיוּ מְיֻחָדִים הָאַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה יַחַד
and this is what is stated in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah (beginning of ch. 3): "I revere [out of joy]," signifying that love and awe were unified harmoniously together.
וְזֶהוּ פֵּרוּשׁ: "בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ, וּרְחִימוּ וּדְחִילוּ"
This explains the dual formulations found in prayer: "in awe and love," and "in love and awe":
תְּחִלָּה "דְּחִילוּ" קוֹדֶמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַרְגָּשַׁת חַיֵּי עוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ וְשׁוֹכֵן בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ "רְחִימוּ"

initially "awe" (d'chilu) takes precedence [bottom-up], arising from the inner sensation of the eternal life that He planted within us and which dwells in our midst, followed subsequently by the ascent into "love" (r'chimu);
וְאַחַר כָּךְ, כְּשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג תּוֹסֶפֶת הַהַשָּׂגָה, וְחוֹזֵר וְיוֹרֵד מִלְּמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה, אָז "רְחִימוּ" קוֹדֶמֶת
and thereafter, once one attains higher divine illumination and re-descends from Above to below [integrating transcendent light into the world], "love" (r'chimu) takes precedence;
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ, וְיָדוּעַ לַיּוֹדְעִים
and this is not the place to elaborate further, as it is known to those versed in wisdom.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן אֵצֶל הַמְּקֻבָּלִים: בְּשִׁלּוּב הַשֵּׁמוֹת, עַל הָרֹב אוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה קוֹדְמִים כְּסֵדֶר יְרִידַת הַהַשָּׂגָה
This also mirrors the Kabbalistic practice in interweaving the Names: most often the letters of Havayah are written first, reflecting the top-down descent of divine illumination;
וְלִפְעָמִים אוֹתִיּוֹת אַדְנוּת קוֹדְמִים כְּסֵדֶר הָעֲבוֹדָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ
while at times the letters of Adnut are written first, reflecting the bottom-up sequence of human spiritual ascent; and this is not the place to expand upon it.
וְהִנֵּה זֶהוּ עִנְיַן מִשְׁכָּן וּמִקְדָּשׁ
Behold, this is the inner distinction between the Tabernacle (Mishkan) and the Holy Temple (Mikdash):
מִשְׁכָּן רָצָה לוֹמַר שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹכֵנוּ, וְזֶה עֲשָׂאוֹ מֹשֶׁה
Mishkan (dwelling) signifies the indwelling presence of Hashem, Blessed be He, within our midst, and this was fashioned through Moses;
כִּי מֵעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הִתְחִיל זֶה הָאוֹר לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹכֵן וּמְקַשְׁקֵשׁ כְּפַעֲמוֹן בְּקֶרֶב לֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
for from the moment of the Giving of the Torah, this divine light began to abide and resonate like a bell within the inner heart of the Children of Israel.
וּמִקְדָּשׁ הוּא לְשׁוֹן קְדֻשָּׁה וְהַבְדָּלָה, וְהוּא הַרְגָּשַׁת הַנִּבְדָּל
Mikdash (Sanctuary), by contrast, stems from the root of holiness (kedushah) and transcendence/separation, representing the conscious perception of the Transcendent;
עַל יְדֵי שְׁלֵמוּת הָעֲבוֹדָה אָנוּ מַשְׁכִּינִים וּמַרְגִּישִׁים בְּתוֹכֵנוּ גַּם אוֹר הַמֻּפְלָא וְהַנִּבְדָּל מֵהַשָּׂגַת כָּל רַעְיוֹן
through the ultimate perfection of spiritual service, we cause even that wondrous, transcendent Light which surpasses all human conception to dwell and be palpably sensed within us.
זֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ "בַּיִת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (פְּסָחִים דַּף פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)
This embodies the spiritual level of our forefather Jacob, peace be upon him, who termed the Sanctuary a "House" (Bayit), as our Sages of blessed memory stated in Pesachim (88a);
כִּידוּעַ מַדְרֵגַת "תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" הוּא שֵׁם הַהַוָּיָ״ה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בַּיִת קָבוּעַ
for as is known, the attribute of "give truth to Jacob" corresponds to the transcendent Name Havayah, which constitutes a permanent, enduring house.
[לָכֵן בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הוֹגֶה שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה בְּאוֹתִיּוֹתָיו, וְכֵן הַכֹּהֲנִים בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ]
[Therefore, in the Holy Temple, the High Priest would pronounce the Name Havayah according to its letters, and likewise the priests in the Sanctuary,]
שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גְּבוּל מִקְרֵי אֹהֶל עֲרַאי, שֶׁבְּהִשְׁתַּלֵּם הַגְּבוּל אֵינֶנּוּ
because anything possessing temporal bounds is termed a temporary tent (ohel arai), which ceases to exist once its bounded allotment is exhausted:
[וּלְכָךְ מִשְׁכַּן שִׁילֹה "אֹהֶל" וְכוּלֵי בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר מֵעִנְיַן מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג

[and for this reason the Mishkan of Shiloh is called a "tent" and stood in the portion of Joseph, corresponding to what we wrote elsewhere regarding the concept of Mashiach ben Yosef who is destined to be slain;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֶּן־דָּוִד "חַיִּים שָׁאַל נָתַתָּ לּוֹ", כְּמוֹ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת (תַּעֲנִית דַּף ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ]

unlike Mashiach ben David, concerning whom Scripture states, "He asked life of You, and You gave it to him," mirroring our forefather Jacob who "did not die" (Ta'anit 5b); and this is not the place to expand upon it.]
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם לָעַד, זֶה נִבְנָה עַל יְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
By contrast, an enduring structure that is established and eternal was built through King Solomon, peace be upon him
[שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן שׁוֹמְמִין, בִּקְדֻשָּׁתָן הֵן, דִּקְדֻשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַמִּשְׁכָּן]
[for "even though they are desolate, they remain in their holiness," as the initial sanctification consecrated the Temple Mount for all eternity, which was not the case with the temporary Mishkan];
וּמְעֻתָּד עַל יְדֵי מְשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד, שֶׁבִּימֵיהֶם נִשְׁתַּלְּמָה מַלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הַשְּׁלֵמוּת, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵמוּת קִבּוּץ הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכָל הָעַמִּים יִנְהֲרוּ אֲלֵיהֶם

and its ultimate fruition is designated to unfold through Mashiach ben David, in whose days the sovereignty of Israel attains absolute perfection, which constitutes the complete gathering of the collective of Israel (Knesset Yisrael), when all the nations of the world will stream unto them.
וְהוּא בֵּרוּר מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאַדְנוּתוֹ בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם
This brings about the definitive clarification of His Sovereignty, Blessed be He, and His Lordship across the entire world;
כִּי רוֹמְמוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רוֹמְמוּת הִתְגַּלּוּת כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם בָּעוֹלָם כַּאֲשֶׁר עוֹבְדָיו מִתְרוֹמְמִים
for the elevation of Israel is itself the exalted manifestation of Heaven's glory in the world when His servants are uplifted,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִלָּה דַּף כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳): "גָּלוּ לְבָבֶל, גָּלְתָה שְׁכִינָה" וְכוּלֵי, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל דִּשְׁכִינָה הַיְנוּ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
as taught in Megillah (29a): "When they were exiled to Babylonia, the Shechinah was exiled," etc., and as noted above, the Shechinah corresponds to Knesset Yisrael.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יִשְׂרָאֵל נִבְנִים לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁלְוָה שְׁלֵמָה, מִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְגַּלֵּית עַל שְׁלֵמוּתָהּ
And when Israel is restored to dwell in consummate tranquility, the divine attribute of His Kingship is revealed in its full perfection;
הַיְנוּ כְּפִי הָאֶפְשָׁרִי לְהִצְטַמְצֵם הַכָּרַת הַחַיִּים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֶצֶם הַחַיִּים, בְּלִבּוֹת כָּל נִבְרְאֵי הָעוֹלָם
that is, to the maximum extent that the conscious awareness of divine vitality—which constitutes the very core of existence—can be channeled and internalized within the hearts of all created beings;
וְכֻלָּם מַכִּירִים וּמְעִידִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ אָדוֹן וּמוֹשֵׁל בַּכֹּל
and all will recognize and bear witness that there is one Master and Sovereign over all existence.
וּשְׁלֵמוּת חֵלֶק הַחַיִּים שֶׁבַּלֵּב הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשַׁת כֹּחַ שֵׁם הַהַוָּיָ״ה
Furthermore, the perfection of that inner spark of life within the heart is achieved through sensing the transcendent reality of Havayah,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְהַוֶּה הַכֹּל, וְהוּא מְמַלֵּא כָּל עָלְמִין וְסוֹבֵב כָּל עָלְמִין
meaning the direct realization that Hashem brings all into being (mehaveh hakol), filling all worlds (Memaleh Kol Almin) and encompassing all worlds (Sovev Kol Almin);
עַל יְדֵי הַרְגָּשָׁה זוֹ בְּיֶתֶר עֹז הוּא שְׁלֵמוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמִדַּת מַלְכוּתוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
through feeling this truth with fortified strength, the perfection of Knesset Yisrael and the attribute of His Kingship is actualized, as stated above.
נִמְצָא: שְׁלֵמוּת מִדַּת הַמַּלְכוּת הַנִּכֶּרֶת בְּלֵב הַנִּבְרָאִים, כַּאֲשֶׁר יְעִידוּן וְיַגִּידוּן כֻּלָּם כְּאֶחָד כִּי הַוָּיָ״ה אֶחָד
Thus we find: the perfection of the attribute of Kingship (Malchut) becomes apparent within the hearts of created beings when all unanimously testify and proclaim that Havayah is One;
שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית כָּל רִבּוּי הַחַיּוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁמִּתְדַּבֵּק יוֹתֵר בִּמְקוֹר הַחַיִּים, וְאָז נִבְנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
for this is the ultimate summit of all intensified vitality in the heart—cleaving ever more deeply to the Source of Life—whereupon the Holy Temple (Beit HaMikdash) is built;
רָצָה לוֹמַר מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ לְאוֹר הַשֵּׁם שֶׁהָיָה, הֹוֶה, וְיִהְיֶה, וְלֹא דִּירַת עֲרַאי וּמוּגְבֶּלֶת בַּזְּמָן
which signifies an eternal, permanent abode for the Light of Hashem Who "was, is, and will be," rather than a temporary and temporally restricted residence.
וְ"אַשְׁכְּחַן מִשְׁכָּן דְּאִיקְרֵי מִקְדָּשׁ" וְכוּלֵי, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַכֹּל אֶחָד, יָחִיד וּמְיֻחָד
And regarding the Talmudic premise, "We find that the Tabernacle was called a Sanctuary," etc., this teaches that in absolute truth both dimensions are one, unified and singular;
וְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין מִשְׁכָּן לְמִקְדָּשׁ הוּא רַק לַנִּבְרָאִים
and the perceived distinction between Mishkan (immanence) and Mikdash (transcendence) exists solely from the vantage point of created beings,
אֲבָל אַשְׁכְּחַן בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה דַּעַת לָאָדָם שֶׁהַכֹּל אֶחָד, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
whereas we find in the Torah—which imparts true divine insight to man—that in ultimate truth all is fundamentally One, as explained above.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה נִתְיַסְּדָה כָּל מַסֶּכֶת עֵירוּבִין וְלִמּוּדֶיהָ: לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד

And according to this foundational approach, the entire Tractate of Eruvin and its teachings were established: to transform the public domain (Reshut HaRabim / the realm of apparent multiplicity and division) into the single, unified domain of the One (Reshut HaYachid).
וְדָבָר זֶה תִּקְּנוֹ שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְעָשָׂה לַתּוֹרָה אָזְנַיִם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֵירוּבִין דַּף כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)
This enactiment was instituted by King Solomon, peace be upon him—the builder of the Holy Temple—who fashioned metaphorical handles/ears (oznayim) for the Torah (as stated in Eruvin 21b),
רָצָה לוֹמַר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה, שֶׁמִּצְוֹת הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ בְּמַעֲשֶׂה
meaning accessible handles to grasp, given that the commandments of the Torah are thoroughly embedded in physical action;
וּמִשְׁלֵי בַּלֵּב, שֶׁהוּא רְמִיזַת כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה וְהַמְּכֻוָּן בָּהֶם
while his Book of Proverbs (Mishlei) speaks directly to the heart, alluding to the inner significance of all actions prescribed by the Torah and their intended mystical focus;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (רֵישׁ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה) שֶׁעַל יָדָם אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and as stated in Vayikra Rabbah (and at the opening of Shir HaShirim Rabbah), that through these parables and enactments a person arrives at the true comprehension of the words of Torah,
רָצָה לוֹמַר לָדַעַת הַמְּכֻוָּן בָּהֶם וְלֶאֱחֹז בָּהֶם
that is, to recognize their divine intent and firmly grasp hold of them.
וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא עַל יְדֵי בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה דְּקָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם, דֻּגְמַת שַׁבָּת
And this perception is attained through the spiritual reality of the Holy Temple, which embodies the permanent and eternally established consciousness, just like the Sabbath;
שֶׁלָּכֵן עָבַד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין דַּף נ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
which is why a non-Jew who observes the Sabbath is liable to death, etc. (as stated in Sanhedrin 58b),
וְאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת דַּף י׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי" וְכוּלֵי
and the Sages noted (Shabbat 10b): "[Hashem said to Moses:] 'I have a precious gift in My treasury... Shabbat is its name,'"
שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה מַתָּנָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
for this sacred reality is an unearned transcendent gift from Above, rather than something generated purely through an arousal from below (itaruta d'letata),
דֻּגְמַת יוֹם טוֹב דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לִזְמַנִּים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פְּסָחִים דַּף ק״יז עַמּוּד ב׳) וּכְפִי שְׁלֵמוּת מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְתַתָּא
unlike the Festivals (Yom Tov), which are sanctified by the calendar court of Israel (as stated in Pesachim 117b) and dependent upon the completeness of their earthly deeds below;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן זֶה קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּם, וּלְכָךְ הוּא רַק לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲשֶׁר "חֵלֶק הַשֵּׁם עַמּוֹ"
whereas the Sabbath is inherently fixed and eternal, and is therefore reserved exclusively for the Children of Israel, regarding whom it is said: "For Hashem's portion is His people."
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הוּא לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲבָל לְעֶצֶם שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה: "אִם צָדַקְתָּ, מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ"

For all active human service pertains to rectifying and building the vessel of Knesset Yisrael (the immanent Shechinah), but relative to the essential transcendent Reality of Havayah, Scripture declares: "If you are righteous, what do you give Him?";
כִּי מִצַּד הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר הַמִּתְפַּשֵּׁט עַד אֵין קֵץ הוּא הַשְּׁבִיתָה מִמַּעֲשִׂים
since from the perspective of that absolute, infinite Divine Oneness expanding without end, the true state is complete cessation from work (shevitah).
וְזֶהוּ הָאֲחִיזָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁלֵי
And this is the grasping of the words of Torah facilitated through Solomon's Mishlei;
[וְזֶהוּ "יִשְׂמַח מֹשֶׁה בְּמַתְּנַת חֶלְקוֹ"
[and this is the esoteric depth of the Sabbath prayer: "Moses rejoiced in the gift of his portion,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן י״ג): דְּמֹשֶׁה מִלְּגַו הוּא יַעֲקֹב מִלְּבַר
as explained in the Zohar (Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13): that Moses inwardly is Jacob externally.
רָצָה לוֹמַר דִּבְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב זָכוּ לִקְדֻשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לִהְיוֹת לְבָבָם חֵלֶק שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה וּמִתְפַּשֵּׁט בָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן בְּחִיצוֹנִיּוּת

This means that externally, all Israel—as the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—merited the sanctification of the Sabbath, so that their hearts form a divine portion of Havayah, with that holiness spreading across their outward existence as well;
אֲבָל בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הוּא רַק מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁהוּא חֵלֶק הַדַּעַת שֶׁל כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּידוּעַ
yet on the innermost plane it is experienced specifically through Moses, who represents the collective faculty of divine consciousness (Da'at) of all Jewish souls, as is known;
וּמִצַּד הַדַּעַת וְהַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים אֶצְלָם הוּא בִּפְנִימִיּוּת לִבָּם וּמוֹחָם גַּם כֵּן הַשָּׂגָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא מַתָּנָה גְּמוּרָה

and from the perspective of this Da'at and the Torah scholars (Talmidei Chachamim), this sublime comprehension is palpably sensed in the innermost core of their hearts and minds as an absolute, unearned gift from Above.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת דַּף ל״א עַמּוּד א׳): "אֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם", שֶׁזֶּה לְבַד מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
It is just as the Sages stated (Shabbat 31a): "The Holy One, Blessed be He, has nothing in His world except awe of Heaven," for reverent awe alone stems directly from man's effort from below,
וּמַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַהֲבָה בָּא לָאָדָם מֵעַצְמוֹ, כִּידוּעַ שֶׁזֶּה מַתָּנָה]
whereas authentic divine love flows into a person spontaneously as an endowed gift from Above, as is known];
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד
and this is not the place to elaborate further.
וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים הוּא מִצַּד הַפֵּרוּד הַנִּגְלֶה
Now, the public domain (Reshut HaRabim) spiritually embodies the dimension of apparent outward division and multiplicity;
וְיֵשׁ עֵצוֹת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נַעֲשֶׂה מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תַּכְלִית הָעֲבוֹדָה

and there exist spiritual methods and halachic remedies to transform this fragmented public realm into the unified domain of the Singular One, as mentioned above, for this is the ultimate purpose of all spiritual service.
וְלָמְדוּ מִפִּתְחוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל
And our Sages derived the legal dimensions of an entranceway from the entrance of the Sanctuary (Heikhal);
רָצָה לוֹמַר כְּסֵדֶר הַכְּנִיסָה אֶל הַהֵיכָל, שֶׁהִיא הַקְּדֻשָּׁה הַשְּׁנִיָּה מִלְּמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה בְּסֵדֶר הָעֶשֶׂר קְדֻשּׁוֹת דְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּכֵלִים

meaning, according to the order of entry into the Heikhal, which constitutes the second highest grade of sanctity descending from top to bottom within the ten progressive degrees of holiness enumerated at the end of the first chapter of Tractate Keilim,
שֶׁרוֹמֶזֶת אֶל קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הַנִּגְלוֹת בַּמּוֹחַ
which alludes to the sanctification of conscious thought revealed in the intellect
[מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים רוֹמֵז לְעֹמֶק הָרָצוֹן וְרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בְּפֵרוּשׁ מִשְׁנָה דְּשָׁם]
[whereas the Holy of Holies (Kodesh HaKodashim) symbolizes the transcendent depth of primal Will and the earliest root of Thought, as I have written elsewhere in expounding the Mishnah there],
שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָסִים לְשָׁם שֶׁלֹּא רְחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
into which priests may not enter without washing their hands and feet;
רָצָה לוֹמַר מְנֻקֶּה בִּכְלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
meaning that one must be thoroughly cleansed and purified in one's instruments of physical action;
שֶׁזֶּה גַּם כֵּן נְטִילַת יָדַיִם שֶׁתִּקֵּן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁיִּסֵּד הַהֵיכָל
and this likewise corresponds to the ritual washing of hands (Netilat Yadayim) instituted by King Solomon, peace be upon him, who founded the Holy Temple;
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּסֵּד קְדֻשָּׁה זוֹ [עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַנֶּאֱמָר: "אַבָּא יָסַד בְּרַתָּא"]
meaning that he firmly established this level of holiness (in accordance with the Kabbalistic axiom: "The Father established the Daughter" / transcendent wisdom structuring the lower realm),
וּכְמִשְׁנָתָהּ, שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ עִנְיַן עֵירוּבִין
and according to its precise Mishnaic teachings, which themselves constitute the inner reality of the laws of Eruvin;
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ כָּעֵת עוֹד
and this is not the place to elaborate on this any further at present.
[ה] "הֱוֵי זָהִיר בִּמְלַאכְתְּךָ, שֶׁמְּלַאכְתְּךָ" וְכוּלֵי (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ג עַמּוּד א׳)

[5] "Be meticulous in your craft, for your craft [is the work of Heaven]" etc. (Eruvin 13a): כִּידוּעַ דְּהַתּוֹרָה צִיּוּר וּדְפוּס כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א׳ — for as is known, the Torah serves as the architect's blueprint and master mold for all of Creation, as recorded in Bereishit Rabbah (chapter 1); כִּי הוּא מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל חֶלְקֵי הַנִּבְרָאִים, כְּלָלֵיהֶם וּפְרָטֵיהֶם וְכָל שִׁנּוּיֵיהֶם — for it is the foundational wellspring of life for every facet of created beings—their general categories, their specific details, and all their diverse variations; אֶחָד לֹא נֶעְדָּר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה חֵלֶק עַצְמוּת חַיּוּתוֹ בְּתוֹךְ דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה — not a single entity is lacking whose essential spark of vitality is not embedded within the words of the Torah. וְכִידוּעַ זֶה, וְאֵין כָּאן מְקוֹמוֹ לְבָאֵר הַדְּבָרִים בַּאֲרִיכוּת לַהַסְבִּירָם אֶל אֹזֶן שׁוֹמַעַת — This principle is well known, and this is not the place to elaborate on these matters at length to unpack them for an attentive ear; וְזֶה עִנְיַן "כִּתְבוּ [לָכֶם אֶת] הַשִּׁירָה" [הַזֹּאת], וְרָצָה לוֹמַר כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ — and this explains the commandment: "Now write down [for yourselves] this song (shirah)," which our Sages interpret as referring to the entire Torah in its entirety. וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן זֶמֶר וָשִׁיר, דְּעַל זֶה נֶעֱנַשׁ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹטָה (דַּף ל״ה עַמּוּד א׳) — This does not denote mere lyrical music or melody—an interpretation for which King David, peace be upon him, was rebuked and penalized, as recorded in Sotah (35a) [for referring to the statutes as "songs"]; רַק הוֹרָאַת "שִׁיר" דָּבָר הַמַּקִּיף סֵדֶר וְהֶקֵּף אֵיזֶה עִנְיָן — rather, the true root meaning of shir denotes an all-encompassing cycle that encloses a complete, ordered system, כְּמוֹ (שַׁבָּת דַּף נ״א עַמּוּד ב׳): "כָּל בַּעֲלֵי הַשִּׁיר יוֹצְאִין בַּשִּׁיר" — as in the Mishnah (Shabbat 51b): "All animals that wear a neck-ring (shir) may go out with their ring"; וְכֵן זֶמֶר וְנִגּוּן מַקִּיף כָּל חֶלְקֵי הַתְּנוּעוֹת וְסִדּוּרָם — and likewise, musical melody encompasses and integrates all rhythmic vocal intervals and their structured arrangements. וְשִׁירַת "הַאֲזִינוּ" מַקֶּפֶת כָּל הַקּוֹמוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת, וְסֵדֶר הַהֶקֵּף הַזֶּה נִקְרָא "שִׁירָה" — The song of Ha'azinu circumscribes all the spiritual statures and historic trajectories of the Children of Israel across all generations, and this comprehensive circular order is called shirah; וְכָל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ כּוֹלֶלֶת סֵדֶר הֶקֵּף כָּל הַחַיִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, סֵדֶר חַיּוּתָם שֶׁל כָּל פְּרָטֵי הַנִּבְרָאִים, עַל כֵּן נִקְרֵאת "שִׁירָה" — and the entire Torah encompasses the full cyclic order of all life upon the earth—the structural vitality animating every specific creature—which is why it is titled shirah.
וּבַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה בְּיִחוּד אֵצֶל מִצְוַת "כִּתְבוּ", אֲשֶׁר עִנְיָנָהּ הַגִּלּוּי הַמְּפֹרָשׁ וְנִכָּר לָעַיִן

And in this context specifically, regarding the commandment "Write down" [the mitzvah to write a Sefer Torah], whose inner purpose is to bring forth an explicit revelation that is visible and perceptible to the eyes:
וְהַיְנוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (דַּף ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא" וְכוּלֵי
this aligns with what is taught in the first chapter of Berakhot (6b): "The entire world was created solely [to accompany this person],"
כִּי הָאָדָם הַשָּׁלֵם יְסוֹד הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר אֵלָיו מַטְּרַת כָּל חֶלְקֵי חַיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים, וְהוּא כַּמֶּרְכָּז בְּתוֹךְ עֲגֻלָּתָם

for the spiritually perfected person is the foundation of the world (tzaddik yesod olam), to whom the vital currents of all created beings gravitate, functioning as the focal center within their enclosing circumference;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּחֲגִיגָה (דַּף י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳): "עַל עַמּוּד אֶחָד הָעוֹלָם עוֹמֵד, וְצַדִּיק שְׁמוֹ"
and as written in Chagigah (12b): "The world stands upon a single pillar, and its name is Tzaddik."
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם" — מִשֶּׁלָּכֶם, מֵחֵלֶק חַיּוּתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָלַק לוֹ הַשֵּׁם, יִבְחַר וִיגַלֶּה כָּל חֶלְקֵי הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים

And this is the inner depth of "write for yourselves"—from that which is your very own, meaning that from the individualized spark of vitality which Hashem apportioned to him, the righteous person articulates and illuminates the vital life-force animating all creatures,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְבֹרָר וְנִגְלֶה לָעַיִן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְחַיֵּה חַיִּים, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ חַיּוּתָם וְקִיּוּמָם
so that it becomes clarified and visually evident that there is an ultimate Sustainer of Life from Whom all existence draws vitality and enduring preservation.
וּלְכָךְ זֶה מִצְוָה אַחֲרוֹנָה בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא אַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר הִשְׁלִים נַפְשׁוֹ בְּכָל הַשְּׁעָרִים הַקּוֹדְמִים

For this reason, writing the Torah constitutes the 613th and final commandment in the Torah, because this level cannot be actualized until one has perfected one's soul through all preceding spiritual gates,
וְנִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּכָל מִינֵי שְׁלֵמוּת הַנִּבְרָא, שֶׁהוּא כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ, הַכּוֹלֶלֶת חַיֵּי עוֹלָם
achieving every dimension of human spiritual perfection embodied by the entire Torah, which contains eternal life (chayei olam),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּשַׁבָּת (דַּף י׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם נָטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ"
as taught in the first chapter of Shabbat (10a), and as we recite: "and He planted eternal life within our midst."
וְאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלֵּם נַפְשׁוֹ בָּזֶה, אָז יָכוֹל לִכְתֹּב וּלְגַלּוֹת וּלְבָרֵר לַכֹּל
And only once a person's soul has attained this total integration is he able to write, reveal, and clarify this divine reality to all;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "סוֹף דָּבָר [הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע, אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים יְרָא וְאֶת מִצְוֹתָיו שְׁמוֹר] כִּי זֶה כָּל הָאָדָם"
matching the verse at the close of Ecclesiastes: "The end of the matter, [all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments,] for this is the whole of man,"
שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ זֶה הוּא סוֹף דָּבָר, שֶׁ"כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא [אֶלָּא לְצַוֹּת לָזֶה]" וְכוּלֵי
for this ultimate realization is the true "end of the matter"—that "the entire world was created solely to serve this [perfected] soul";
וְעַל תַּכְלִית וּמְכֻוָּן זֶה: "אֶת הָאֱלֹקִים יְרָא"
and toward this ultimate purpose and objective: "Fear God,"
בְּעֹמֶק הַיִּרְאָה כָּל כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִגְלֶה וְנִרְאֶה לְעֵין כֹּל כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹרֵא וּמַנְהִיג שֶׁכָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים חַיּוּתָם מִמֶּנּוּ
penetrating into such depth of reverent awe until it becomes outwardly manifest and visible to every eye that there is a Creator and Guide from Whom all creatures derive their vitality.
נִמְצָא שֶׁמֵּחֵלֶק חַיִּים שֶׁחָלַק לוֹ הַשֵּׁם, גִּלָּה וּבֵרַר הַדָּבָר כִּי יֵשׁ חֵלֶק חַיִּים בְּכָל הַבְּרוּאִים
Thus we find that from the portion of divine life allotted to him by Hashem, the tzaddik reveals and demonstrates that an authentic spark of life exists within all creatures
[שֶׁרַק זֶה הַחַיִּים כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַיֶּה אוֹתָם, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא חַיִּים
[for existence is truly considered "life" only when Hashem, Blessed be He, animates it with holiness, which alone qualifies as real life;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה׳) עַל פַּרְעֹה שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ בֵּין הַמֵּתִים
as expounded in Shemot Rabbah (parashah 5) regarding Pharaoh, who sought the name of Hashem in the necrologies of the dead;
כִּי מַה שֶּׁזּוּלַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא מֵת וְדָבָר בָּטֵל מִן הָעוֹלָם, וְזֶה יָדוּעַ וּמוּבָן]
because whatever severs itself from Hashem is termed spiritually "dead" and an absolute nullity in the world, as is known and understood];
הֲרֵי הַחַיִּים שֶׁבָּהֶם נִתְגַּלּוּ עַל יָדוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְדוֹמָיו, וְזֶה עִנְיַן "כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ" וְכוּלֵי

behold, the divine vitality animating them is revealed through him, as occurred through our forefather Abraham, peace be upon him, and those like him; and this is the inner meaning of "the entire world was created [for this purpose]."
וְזֶהוּ בְּ"סוֹף דָּבָר", אַחַר סוֹף הַשְּׁלֵמוּת הָאֶפְשָׁרִי לָאָדָם, לְכָךְ הוּא סוֹף הַתּוֹרָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
This culmination takes place at the "end of the matter"—following the apex of human spiritual perfection—which is why this mitzvah stands at the very end of the Torah, as noted above.
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עַיֵּן בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ע״ז): מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָמוֹת, אַף צַדִּיקִים
And this is what our Sages of blessed memory taught (see Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 77): "Just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, creates worlds, so too do the tzaddikim";
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַמְּחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית"
as we declare in prayer: "Who in His goodness renews daily, continuously, the work of Creation,"
שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם יֵשׁ בְּרִיאָה מְחֻדֶּשֶׁת, שֶׁלּוּלֵי כֹּחַ חַיִּים חָדָשׁ שֶׁנּוֹתֵן לַבְּרוּאִים בְּכָל יוֹם, הָיָה כְּלֹא הָיָה
for every day witnesses a renewed act of creation, such that without the fresh influx of life bestowed upon creatures daily, all would instantly revert to absolute nothingness.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים, כִּי הַשְׁפָּעוֹת הַחֵלֶק הַחַיִּים לְקִיּוּם הַבְּרוּאִים הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּכִּירִים וּמְגַלִּים בְּבֵרוּר
And this sustaining renewal is also channeled through the tzaddikim, because the divine bestowal of life sustaining created beings flows through their clear recognition and revelation
כִּי רַק חַיֵּי עוֹלָם יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁבָּהֶם הוּא הַמְּחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם
that only the Life of all worlds, blessed be His Name, pulsating within them, gives life to all existence.
וְנִמְצָא נִגְלֶה עַל יָדָם כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם, וְזֶה עַצְמוֹ חַיּוּתָם וְקִיּוּמָם שֶׁעַל יְדֵיהֶם נִגְלָה הַכְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם, וְהָבֵן זֶה
Thus the glory of Heaven is revealed through their agency, and this very revelation of Heaven's glory constitutes the underlying vitality and preservation of all beings; understand this deeply.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "הֱוֵי זָהִיר בִּמְלַאכְתְּךָ", לָדַעַת שֶׁהוּא מְלֶאכֶת שָׁמַיִם
And this is what Rabbi Yishmael meant when he warned: "Be meticulous in your craft," knowing that it is truly the "work of Heaven,"
כְּעִנְיַן "וְאַתָּה תִּשְׁמַע הַשָּׁמַיִם", דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רָצָה לוֹמַר מְלָאכָה שְׁמֵימִית
evocative of the phrase, "and You shall hear from Heaven," where "Heaven" is a designation for Hashem, Blessed be He, signifying a truly heavenly, divine craft;
שֶׁעִנְיַן כְּתִיבַת הַתּוֹרָה הוּא עִנְיַן בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָמוֹת כֻּלָּם, דֻּגְמַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
for the sacred craft of writing a Torah scroll mirrors the actual creation of all worlds, patterned after the Holy One, Blessed be He, as explained above.
שֶׁ"אִם אַתָּה [מְחַסֵּר אוֹת אַחַת אוֹ מְיַתֵּר אוֹת אַחַת, נִמְצָא אַתָּה מַחֲרִיב אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ]" וְכוּלֵי
For "if you [omit a single letter or add a single letter, you turn out to destroy the entire world]," etc.:
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁסֵּדֶר הַבְּרִיאָה מְסֻדֶּרֶת עַל אֹפֶן הַיּוֹתֵר מְתֻקָּן מֵאֵת הָאֻמָּן הַמֻּפְלָא, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for as is known, the cosmic order of Creation was constructed in the most consummate, calibrated harmony by the Master Craftsman, Hashem, Blessed be He.
וּכְמוֹ הַמּוֹרֶה שָׁעוֹת הַמְּסֻדָּר מִן הָאֻמָּן עַל אֹפֶן הָרָאוּי
Consider the analogy of a mechanical clock assembled by a master artisan in precise fashion:
אִם יְשַׁנּוּ סִדְרוֹ, אוֹ יִגְרְעוּ, אוֹ יוֹסִיפוּ, יִתְקַלְקֵל כָּל מְכֻוַּן הַבִּנְיָן, אֲשֶׁר הוּא רַק כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּסֵּדֶר הַמְּכֻוָּן הַהוּא

if someone alters its internal mechanisms, subtracting a gear or adding an extra cog, the entire functional objective of the mechanism is ruined, since its design functions solely when aligned in that exact calibration.
וְכָךְ סֵדֶר הָעוֹלָם: הֲיֵשׁ אֻמָּן גָּדוֹל מִבּוֹרְאוֹ?
And such is the order of the cosmos: is there any artisan greater than its Creator?
מִסְּתָמָא סֵדֶר חֶלְקֵי כֹּחוֹת הַחַיִּים שֶׁבּוֹ הֵם עַל סֵדֶר הַמְּכֻוָּן בְּיוֹתֵר, וְכֻלּוֹ הֶקֵּף סֵדֶר אֶחָד, אֲשֶׁר עַל שְׁמָם נִקְרָאת הַתּוֹרָה "שִׁירָה" כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

Self-evidently, the distribution of vital life-forces within it is calibrated with ultimate precision, forming one continuous, integrated system, by reason of which the Torah is titled shirah (song/ring), as noted above;
שֶׁהִיא כְּטַבַּעַת אוֹ אֶצְעָדָה הַמַּקִּיף סֵדֶר שָׁלֵם כְּהָעֲגֻלָּה, שֶׁהוּא סֵדֶר שָׁלֵם זֶה רָצוּף אַחַר זֶה, חֵלֶק אַחַר חֵלֶק
for the Torah is like a ring or bracelet encircling a complete whole like an unbroken circle, which forms a harmonious sequence linked link-to-link, component by component.
וְאִם יֶחְסַר קְצָת מִמֶּנּוּ, הֲרֵי נֶחֱרַב הַסֵּדֶר כֻּלּוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעַתָּה סֵדֶר שָׁלֵם
If even a minute detail is missing from it, the entire systemic balance is destroyed, for it no longer constitutes a complete order.
וְזֶה מִצְוַת "בַּל תֹּסֵף" וּ"בַל תִּגְרַע"
And this is the inner meaning of the biblical injunctions against adding to or subtracting from the commandments (Bal Tosef and Bal Tigra),
שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק יְסוֹד וְעַמּוּד שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם נִשְׁעָן עָלָיו, שֶׁהוּא הַמְּבָרֵר וּמְגַלֶּה כָּל סֵדֶר חֶלְקֵי הַחַיִּים שֶׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the tzaddik is the pillar upon whom the entire world rests, who articulates and reveals the precise order of all life-sparks created by Hashem, Blessed be He;
וְזֶהוּ כְּתִיבַת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה בְּלִי חִסָּרוֹן וּבְלִי יִתְרוֹן, רַק כְּפִי סֵדֶר הַחַיּוּת שֶׁיִּסֵּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this constitutes the sacred writing of the entire Torah without deficit and without excess, mirroring strictly the exact architecture of vitality established by Hashem, Blessed be He.
[ו] "וְאָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי, וְקַנְקַנְתּוֹם [שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁאֲנִי מֵטִיל לְתוֹךְ הַדְּיוֹ]" וְכוּלֵי, "לִזְבוּב" וְכוּלֵי (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ג עַמּוּד א׳)

[6] "And I said to him: I have one ingredient, and vitriol/copperas (kankantom) is its name, which I put into the ink," etc., "[and if] a fly [comes and blots out a letter, it remains erased]" etc. (Eruvin 13a): פֵּרוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "זְבוּבֵי מָוֶת יַבְאִישׁ" וְגוֹמֵר — the meaning corresponds to Scripture stating: "Dead flies make the perfumer's ointment stink," etc., וּבְפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ס״א עַמּוּד א׳): "יֵצֶר הָרָע דּוֹמֶה לִזְבוּב" — and in the chapter HaRo'eh (Berakhot 61a): "The evil inclination (yetzer hara) resembles a fly"; וְהוּא רוֹמֵז לְקִלְקוּל וְהֶעְדֵּר — and it alludes spiritually to ruin, defect, and privation/absence of light.
וּבְכֹחוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה לוֹמַר עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר וְכוּלֵי (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
In the spiritual power of Rabbi Meir was the ability to declare the ritually impure to be pure, etc. (Eruvin 13b);
רָצָה לוֹמַר לְגַלּוֹת חַיּוּת שֶׁבַּבְּרוּאִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שׁוּם קִלְקוּל
meaning, to uncover the hidden divine vitality within all creatures to the extent that no ruin or imperfection remains,
וְגַם הַטֻּמְאָה וְהַקִּלְקוּל, גַּם בּוֹ חַיּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְטָהֳרָה
and that even within impurity and defect, there resides the animating vitality of Hashem, Blessed be He, and ultimate purity.
וְכֵן לֶעָתִיד: "וְגָר זְאֵב עִם כֶּבֶשׂ" וְגוֹמֵר
And so will it be in the ultimate Future: "And the wolf shall dwell with the lamb," etc.;
וְהַיְנוּ כִּי עִנְיַן טוֹב וָרָע וְטֻמְאָה וְטָהֳרָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְקָבַע כֵּן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זֶה טוֹב
for the dichotomy of good and evil, impurity and purity, was deliberately established and fashioned by Hashem, Blessed be He, decreeing that this shall be good,
וְיִהְיֶה מְקוֹם מְצִיאוּת לָרַע לְהִגָּלוֹת לְמַרְאִית הָעַיִן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, הַמַּרְאֶה הַפֵּרוּד וְהָרִבּוּי וְהֶעְדֵּר גִּלּוּי הַיִּחוּד
and granting an existential realm for evil to appear to the external eye in this world, which projects division, multiplicity, and the concealment of Divine Unity.
וְהוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הִצְטַמְצֵם הַטּוֹב בִּגְבוּל וְגָדֵר: "עַד פֹּה תָבוֹא", בְּלִי הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת לְאֵין קֵץ
This emerges when the Good is contracted (tzimtzum) into precise borders and fences—"thus far shall you come"—without infinite expansion,
נִשְׁאַר חוּץ לַגְּבוּל מְקוֹם גִּלּוּי הַהֵפֶךְ
leaving beyond that defined perimeter a conceptual space wherein its opposite can become apparent.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר יִתְבָּרֵר הָאֱמֶת לְעֵין כֹּל, וְיוּחְזַר הַדָּבָר לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
But when the absolute truth becomes clarified before the eyes of all, and reality is restored to its pristine root as it was before the world was created,
הַיִּחוּד הַבָּרוּר לְעֵין כֹּל, וְשֶׁהַכֹּל בְּרָצוֹן אֶחָד יָחִיד וּמְיֻחָד, וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ לוֹ
the absolute Oneness will be visibly transparent to all, revealing that everything stems from the singular, unified Divine Will without any dividing barrier;
מַה מָּקוֹם לְטֻמְאָה וְטָהֳרָה, וְאִסּוּר וְהֶתֵּר, וְטוֹב וָרָע מֵעַתָּה?
what place remains then for the categories of impurity and purity, prohibition and permission, or good and evil?
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים: "כִּי בַיּוֹם הַזֶּה יְכַפֵּר [עֲלֵיכֶם לְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם]" וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁאֵין מָקוֹם לַחֵטְא
And this is the inner mystery of Yom Kippur: "For on this day He shall effect atonement [upon you to purify you]," etc., where at that elevated root-source sin has no standing or reality.
וּמִזֶּה נִצְמָחִים הָעֵצוֹת לְתַקֵּן אֶת הַחֲטָאִים וְקִלְקוּלִים
And from this primordial perspective stem the spiritual pathways to rectify sins and spiritual defects,
שֶׁיְּבֹרַר כָּל כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע כִּי לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם קִלְקוּל כְּלָל
clarifying them so thoroughly until it is realized that no lasting damage ever truly existed at that transcendent core,
וְהַדְּבָרִים אֲרֻכִּים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
and these matters are elaborated at length elsewhere.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פֶּרֶק כ׳): בְּתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה כָּתוּב "כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר"
And this is what is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah ch. 20): "In the Torah scroll of Rabbi Meir, it was written 'garments of light' (or spelled with an Alef instead of Ayin)";
כִּי הַכָּתְנוֹת הֵם הַלְּבוּשִׁים הַמַּעֲלִימִים אֶת הַגּוּף
for garments are coverings that normally conceal the physical body,
וְ"אוֹר" בְּאָלֶ״ף הַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם דֶּרֶךְ הַלְּבוּשׁ מֵאִיר וּמַזְהִיר הַגּוּף
yet "light" spelled with an Alef signifies that even through the concealing garment, the essential light shines and radiates through;
וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ
and this is not the place to elaborate further.
וְזֶהוּ עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר וּמַרְאֶה לוֹ פָּנִים
And this was his spiritual ability to declare the impure to be pure by demonstrating its "face" (panim / inner aspect);
כִּי הַפָּנִים עֶצֶם הַכָּרַת הַדָּבָר, כְּמוֹ (יְבָמוֹת דַּף ק״כ עַמּוּד א׳): "אֵין מְעִידִין אֶלָּא עַל פַּרְצוּף פָּנִים"
for the face represents the essential identity and core reality of an entity, as stated in Yevamot (120a): "Testimony is accepted only based upon the facial features."
וְעַל טָהוֹר טָמֵא
And conversely, [Rabbi Meir's ability to demonstrate] regarding the pure that it is impure:
רָצָה לוֹמַר כִּי יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ס״א עַמּוּד א׳): "יֵצֶר הָרָע" וְכוּלֵי "וְיוֹשֵׁב עַל שְׁנֵי מִפְתְּחֵי הַלֵּב"
meaning, as is known from what the Sages stated (Berakhot 61a): "The evil inclination... sits upon the two chambers/entrances of the heart";
כִּי "לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ, וְלֵב [כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ]"
for "a wise man's heart directs him to his right, while the heart [of a fool directs him to his left],"
וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם לֵאמֹר עַל יָמִין שֶׁהוּא שְׂמֹאל וְעַל שְׂמֹאל שֶׁהוּא יָמִין, וְאוֹמֵר עַל טָהוֹר טָמֵא

and the evil inclination positions itself over both entrances to claim that right is left and that left is right, misrepresenting that which is pure as impure [causing a person to push away that which is holy].
וּבְיַד רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן וְלוֹמַר שֶׁגַּם בָּזֶה לֹא חָטָא
Yet in Rabbi Meir's spiritual capacity was the ability to delve even here, demonstrating that at the deepest level, the person had not sinned even in this,
וְדָבָר זֶה עָמוֹק בַּחָכְמָה, שֶׁגַּם לְהַרְחָקַת דָּבָר טוֹב יִהְיֶה תִּקּוּן
and this matter is profoundly deep in wisdom: that even for mistakenly distancing oneself from a good thing there is a spiritual rectification,
שֶׁגַּם זֶה נִתְקָן לְמַפְרֵעַ שֶׁהוּא כֵּן, אַף שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר בֶּאֱמֶת
such that even this is rectified retroactively as having unfolded deliberately as it should, despite the object being genuinely pure;
מִצַּד מַדְרֵגָתוֹ הָיָה יָכוֹל לְבָרֵר גַּם אֶת זֶה וּלְתַקְּנוֹ לְמַפְרֵעַ
from the lofty vantage of his spiritual stature, he was able to elucidate and clarify even this defect and rectify it retroactively.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם"
And this is what the Talmud meant there (Eruvin 13b): "It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being [that in Rabbi Meir's generation there was none like him]":
כִּידוּעַ דִּבְרֵי הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל "בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם", הוּא "רֵישָׁא דְּלָא אִתְיַדַּע"

for as is known from the teachings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory, the phrase "Blessed is He Who spoke and the world came into being" designates Reisha D'lo Ityada (the Unknowable Supernal Head / the primordial transcendent Source);
פֵּרוּשׁ רֵאשִׁית וּמְקוֹר הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ נוֹדָע וְנִגְלֶה
meaning the very genesis and primal origin of Thought, which remains utterly unknown and unrevealed;
כִּי הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה כְּבָר יֵשׁ לָהּ תְּפִיסָה מַה בַּמּוֹחַ, וְהִיא נִפְרֶדֶת מִן עֶצֶם הַמְּחַשֵּׁב, וַהֲרֵי הִיא נִגְלֵית וְנוֹדַעַת לַמְּחַשֵּׁב
for thought already possesses a degree of cognitive grasp within the mind, having separated somewhat from the very essence of the thinker, and is thus apparent and known to the thinker himself;
אֲבָל מְקוֹר הַמּוֹלִיד הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְרֵאשִׁיתָהּ, דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ נִגְלֶה וְנוֹדָע כְּלָל
but the transcendent wellspring that births thought and stands at its genesis is not manifest or knowable at all,
כִּי הוּא כְּמוֹ מְמֻצָּע בֵּין עֶצֶם הַמְּחַשֵּׁב וּבֵין הַנִּפְרָד מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁהִיא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה, וְהוּא כְּמוֹ סוֹף הַמַּאֲצִיל וּמְחַשֵּׁב וְרֵאשִׁית הַנֶּאֱצָל

because it serves as an intermediary between the essence of the thinker and that which extends from him (the conscious thought), standing, as it were, at the culmination of the Emanator/Thinker and the inception of the emanated thought.
וְעַל רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הַזּוֹ בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם
And concerning this primordial inception of Divine Thought at the creation of the cosmos
[דְּעִנְיַן זוֹ הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה וְהַפְּעֻלָּה הוּא הַכּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל שְׁמוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ וּתְאָרָיו וְכָל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית וּמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהִיא רַק מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה כִּידוּעַ]

[for this category of Thought and Action encompasses all of His Holy Names, divine titles, the Work of Creation (Ma'aseh Bereishit), and the Work of the Chariot (Ma'aseh Merkavah), all of which relate solely from the perspective of Creation, as is known],
נֶאֱמַר הַלָּשׁוֹן: "שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם"
the specific phrasing was used: "Who spoke (she'amar) and the world came into being."
כִּי "בִּדְבַר הַשֵּׁם שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ", וְדִבּוּר הוּא בְּקוֹל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף רכ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳), וְזֶהוּ הָעֲשִׂיָּה

For "by the word (d'var) of Hashem the heavens were made," and "speech" (dibur) emerges audibly with a voice, as written in the Zohar (Vol. III, 227b), representing physical actualization and action (Asiyah);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אֲמִירָה בִּלְחִישָׁה, זֶהוּ רֵאשִׁית וּמְקוֹר הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
whereas "saying" (amirah) in a whisper corresponds to the inception and source of Thought,
שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה כְּבָר הִיא בְּגִלּוּי עַל כָּל פָּנִים לַמְּחַשֵּׁב, אֲבָל בִּלְחִישָׁה גְּמוּרָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַשְׁמִיעַ גַּם לְאָזְנָיו
since thought is already manifest at least to the thinker himself, whereas an absolute whisper that does not reach even one's own ears
הִיא "רֵישָׁא דְּלָא אִתְיַדַּע", שֶׁנִּקְרָא "דְּלָא יָדַע וְלָא אִתְיַדַּע" כִּידוּעַ
embodies Reisha D'lo Ityada, which is described as that which "neither knows nor is known," as is known.
וְעַל יְדֵי הַחְזָרַת הַדְּבָרִים לַמָּקוֹר הַזֶּה
And through elevating and restoring matters back to this transcendent Source,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר כָּל כָּךְ בֵּרוּר גָּמוּר אַחְדוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning, that the absolute Unity of Hashem, Blessed be He, is elucidated with such total clarity
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִפְרָד אַף כְּגֶדֶר פְּרִידַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה מִן הַמְּחַשֵּׁב, רַק בְּיִחוּד עֶצֶם כְּיִחוּד רֵישָׁא דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ

that nothing is severed from Him even to the slight extent that a thought separates from the thinker, but rather unites in absolute essential Oneness like the unity at the very summit of that primal Thought;
שֶׁהִיא רֵאשִׁית הַצִּמְצוּם, שֶׁהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עַצְמָהּ כְּבָר הִיא בִּגְבוּל
for that summit is the earliest inception of contraction (tzimtzum), since articulated thought already contains finitude and boundary;
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר יָבוֹא לְהַשִּׂיג הַשָּׂגָה בְּרוּרָה כָּל כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ אֶצְלוֹ מְיֻחָד גַּם עַכְשָׁו כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בִּמְקוֹר רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה
but when one attains an insight so completely lucid that the entire created universe is perceived by him as unified even now, precisely as it was in the primal origin at the inception of Thought,
אָז הוּא בִּלְתִּי גְּבוּל כְּלָל, רַק מְעֻתָּד לָצֵאת בִּגְבוּלִים בִּלְתִּי יְדוּעִים לְאוֹתוֹ מְקוֹר הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עֲדַיִן
then existence is perceived as utterly without boundary, merely destined to emerge in parameters not yet delineated within that primal origin of Thought.
וּלְהַמָּקוֹר וְרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה אֵין נָפְקָא מִנַּהּ אִם לֵאמֹר עַל טָהוֹר טָמֵא אוֹ לְהֵפֶךְ
And from the vantage point of that ultimate Origin and Head of Thought, there is no practical difference (nafka mina) whether declaring the pure to be impure or vice versa;
מִצַּד בֵּרוּר אֲמִתַּת הַיִּחוּד עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה
from the perspective of clarifying the absolute reality of Divine Unity in this profound manner,
הֲרֵי כָּל מַה שֶּׁנַּעֲשָׂה, הַכֹּל הוּא מְיֻחָד לְגַמְרֵי, וְאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר יוֹצֵא מִגְּבוּלִין שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
behold, whatever occurs is entirely and utterly unified with Him, and nothing whatsoever departs from the sovereign boundaries of Hashem, Blessed be He;
וּדְבָרִים אֵלּוּ אֲרֻכִּים בִּמְקוֹמָן בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא
and these deep matters are expounded at length in their appropriate place, with the assistance of Heaven (b'siyata d'shmaya).
וְזֶהוּ "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנַי"
And this is the inner meaning of the statement: "It is revealed and known before Me":
אוֹתָהּ הַמַּדְרֵגָה, שֶׁאֵין בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ
[referring specifically to] that elevated transcendent level, regarding which there was no one in the generation of Rabbi Meir comparable to him in this spiritual rank.
וְגַם רַבִּי הִשִּׂיג קְצָת מִמַּדְרֵגָה זוֹ
And Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] also attained a measure of this lofty level,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם): "הַאי דִּמְחַדַּדְנָא, דַּחֲזִיתֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מֵאַחוֹרָיו"
as recorded in the Talmud there (Eruvin 13b): "The reason that I am sharper [than my colleagues] is that I saw Rabbi Meir from behind";
פֵּרוּשׁ עַל דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל, כְּעִנְיַן "וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי"
the meaning being metaphorical, evocative of the verse stated to Moses: "And you shall see My back,"
עַיֵּן בָּרַמְבַּ״ם פֶּרֶק א׳ מֵהִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר הַשָּׂגָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְבֹרֶרֶת
see Maimonides in Chapter 1 of Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah, where he explains that "seeing from behind" denotes perception that is not fully transparent and clear;
וְכֵן הוּא הִשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגָתוֹ, אֲבָל לֹא בְּהַשָּׂגָה בְּרוּרָה כְּמוֹתוֹ
and so Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] attained his spiritual level, though not with the same total, lucid clarity that Rabbi Meir himself possessed.
וְעִנְיַן "רְאִיָּה" — הַשָּׂגָה, כְּמוֹ "וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה"
And the term "seeing" denotes intellectual/spiritual perception, as in the verse: "And my heart saw much wisdom";
וְכֵן כַּוָּנַת הַקְּרָא דְּ"וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת מוֹרֶיךָ" דְּמַיְיתֵי, רָצָה לוֹמַר עֵינֵי הַשֵּׂכֶל
and likewise the intent of the verse cited there, "And your eyes shall see your teachers," refers to the eyes of the intellect.
וְלָכֵן סָתַם רַבִּי מַתְנִיתִין בְּכָל מָקוֹם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
For this reason, Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] formulated the anonymous, authoritative Mishnah everywhere in accordance with Rabbi Meir;
וְעַיֵּן בְּשִׁלְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת, דְּרַבִּי הוּא דְּאַסְקֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר לֵאמֹר "רַבִּי מֵאִיר" וְלֹא "אֲחֵרִים"

and see the conclusion of Tractate Horayot (13b–14a), where it was Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] who elevated Rabbi Meir by citing him explicitly by name ("Rabbi Meir says") rather than pseudonymously ("Others say");
וְאָמְרוּ: "מִי הֵם שֶׁמֵּימֵיהֶם אָנוּ שׁוֹתִים" וְכוּלֵי
and they declared: "Who are they whose waters we drink [and whose names we do not mention]?" etc.
וּלְכָךְ אָמַר רַבִּי בְּפֶרֶק יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (יוֹמָא דַּף פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳) דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר גַּם לְשֶׁאֵינָן שָׁבִים
And for this very reason, Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] taught in the chapter concerning Yom Kippur (Yoma 85b) that the holy day of Yom Kippur atones even for those who do not repent;
שֶׁיֵּשׁ מָקוֹם לְכַפָּרָה גַּם שֶׁלֹּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה, כְּעִנְיַן "וְחַנֹּתִי אֶת אֲשֶׁר אָחֹן"
[demonstrating] that there exists a transcendent realm of atonement even without active repentance, in the manner of "and I will show grace to whom I show grace,"
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְּדַאי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳)
"even though he is not worthy" (as explained in Berakhot 7a),
דְּהוּא אֲתַר דְּלָא קַיְימָא לִשְׁאֵלָה, דְּהַאי יוֹמָא דְּקָא גָּרֵים לְעוֹרֵר אַחְדוּת הַגְּמוּרָה וּגְלוּיָה עַל אֹפֶן הַנִּזְכָּר
for that is the supernal realm beyond all inquiry (atar d'lo kayma l'she'eila), where the sacred potency of that day itself arouses absolute, revealed Oneness in the manner described above.
דְּלָכֵן הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הוֹגֶה הַשֵּׁם בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם
Therefore, the High Priest would utter the ineffable Divine Name on that very day;
דְּשֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה וַהֲגִיָּתוֹ מוֹרֶה עַל הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְמַעְלָה רֹאשׁ
for the Name Havayah and its literal enunciation denote absolute Oneness, as was thoroughly elucidated above.
וּמִשּׁוּם דְּלָא חַזְיֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִקַּמֵּיהּ
Yet because Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] did not behold Rabbi Meir "from the front,"
רָצָה לוֹמַר הַשָּׂגָה בְּרוּרָה כָּל כָּךְ כְּמַדְרֵגַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר, לָכֵן לֹא הִשִּׂיג לוֹמַר זֶה בְּכָל יוֹם עַל טָמֵא וְכוּלֵי
meaning a perception so utterly direct and lucid as Rabbi Meir's own stature, he therefore did not attain the capacity to declare daily regarding the impure [that it is pure], etc.
וְהִנֵּה הַהֲלָכָה אֵינוֹ כֵּן, וְלֹא נִקְבַּע הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ
And behold, practical halachic ruling is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir, nor was the law established according to his sublime view,
לְפִי שֶׁבְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם הָיְתָה בְּגֶדֶר וּגְבוּל וּמָקוֹם לִבְחִירָה בְּטוֹב וָרָע וְשָׂכָר וָעֹנֶשׁ
because the creation of this world was purposely structured within parameters, boundaries, and a distinct arena for free-willed choice between good and evil, accompanied by reward and punishment.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ג עַמּוּד א׳): "כְּתָב שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִמְחוֹת בָּעֵינַן"
And this is what Rabbi Yishmael replied to him (Eruvin 13a): "We require script that is capable of being erased";
דְּצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אֶפְשָׁרִיּוּת לִמְחוֹת וְקִלְקוּל הַכְּתָב, וְהַיְנוּ בְּחִירָה בָּרָע וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָקוֹם גַּם לָרָע לְהִמָּצֵא
meaning that there must exist the real possibility of erasure and defect in the writing—which represents the capacity to choose evil, allowing an existential realm wherein evil can actually exist.
שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַדְרָגַת הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא
For this constitutes the operational structure of this physical world as it currently stands,
הֲגַם דִּבְעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין שָׁם בְּחִירָה
even though in the World to Come (Olam HaBa) there is no free choice,
וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין דַּף כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם" — וְלֹא לְמָחָר
as our Sages of blessed memory declared (Eruvin 22a): "'Today to perform them'—and not tomorrow [in the World to Come]";
וּכְמַאן דְּאָמַר (נִדָּה דַּף ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳): "מִצְוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא"
and according to the authority who maintains (Niddah 61b) that "the commandments are destined to be annulled in the Time to Come."
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין דַּף ק״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): "דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אָמְרוּ: כֻּלָּם בָּאִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא"
For this reason our Sages of blessed memory taught (Sanhedrin 104b): "The allegorical interpreters (dorshei reshumot) declared: all of them have a portion in the World to Come";
דְּהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בֶּאֱמֶת בְּלֹא גְּבוּל
because the World to Come is in absolute truth boundless,
