כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהַאֲכַלְתִּיךָ נַחֲלַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִיךָ" — נַחֲלָה בְּלֹא מְצָרִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת דַּף קי״ח עַמּוּד ב׳)
as it is written: "And I will feed you the heritage of Jacob your father"—a boundless heritage without confining borders (as taught in Shabbat 118b);
אֲבָל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה אֵינוֹ כֵּן, וְהוּא בַּעַל גְּבוּל וּזְמַן הַמַּעֲשִׂים, טוֹב וָרָע
but this present world is not so, being defined by boundaries and constituting the temporal arena of human action, demarcated by good and evil.
[ז] וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם): "שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמֹד עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ"
[7] And this is what they meant when they stated (Eruvin 13b): "That his colleagues could not fathom the ultimate depth of his mind":
כִּי לְכָל דַּעַת וְשֵׂכֶל נִבְרָא יֵשׁ סוֹף וּגְבוּל: "עַד פֹּה תָבוֹא"
for every created intellect and mind possesses a terminus and finite boundary—"thus far shall you come"—
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לְדַעְתּוֹ לֹא הָיָה שׁוּם גְּבוּל וְדָבָר שֶׁמַּגְדִּירוֹ
whereas to his transcendent understanding there was no limit whatsoever or defining boundary,
שֶׁנֹּאמַר שֶׁעַד כָּאן תְּחוּם שִׂכְלוֹ, וְדָבָר כָּזֶה לֹא יוּכַל עוֹד לְטַהֵר בְּרֹחַב דַּעְתּוֹ
such that one could say: "up to this point is the perimeter of his intellect, and beyond this he can no longer demonstrate purity through the vast breadth of his mind."
וַעֲמִידָה נִקְרָא כְּשֶׁעוֹמֵד וְאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לֵילֵךְ יוֹתֵר, וְהוּא כְּעוֹמֵד עַל הַגְּבוּל
And a state of "standing" (amidah) is termed when someone halts because he has no further place to walk, positioned directly at the boundary line;
וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ לֹא הָיוּ יְכוֹלִים לַעֲמֹד עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ, כִּי אֵין לוֹ גְּבוּל
therefore they stated that regarding him, they could not "stand" at the end of his intellect, because his perception possessed no boundary;
וּלְכָךְ אֵין הֲלָכָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, דְּאֵין מְטִילִין קַנְקַנְתּוֹם
and therefore the practical halachah was not established in accordance with his view, as mentioned above, meaning that we do not cast vitriol (kankantom / permanent indelible fixative) into the ink,

[וְיֵשׁ לִרְמֹז שֶׁהוּא בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "שֵׁמוֹת", וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (דַּף ז׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) דָּרְשִׁינַן: מֵ"אֲשֶׁר שָׂם שַׁמּוֹת [בָּאָרֶץ]", דִּשְׁמָא קָא גָּרֵים, וְאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (דַּף פ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "רַבִּי מֵאִיר דָּיֵיק בִּשְׁמָא"

[and one may note the esoteric allusion that the numerical value of kankantom equals that of shemot (names), and in the first chapter of Berakhot (7b) the Sages expounded on the verse "who has placed desolations (shamot) in the earth"—read rather as shemot (names)—that a person's name determines destiny, and in Yoma (83b) they stated: "Rabbi Meir was meticulous to discern character through names,"
כִּידוּעַ דְּהַשֵּׁם הוּא חַיּוּת וְכֹחַ הַדָּבָר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
as is known that the name constitutes the essential vitality and animating power of an entity, as written elsewhere;
וְזֶהוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ הָיָה דָּיֵיק בִּשְׁמָא, שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹר חַיָּיו הַפְּרָטִי בַּמָּקוֹר הַכְּלָלִי שֶׁל כָּל הַחַיִּים
and thus Rabbi Meir, from his supreme spiritual vantage, was able to discern the name, linking each individualized root of life back into the all-encompassing Source of all Life;
וְהוּא בְּרֶמֶז הַדְּיוֹ, שֶׁהוּא מָקוֹר הַכּוֹלֵל כָּל אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא כְּלָלוּת הַחַיִּים, וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ]

and this is mirrored in the symbolism of the ink, which represents the unified primordial source encompassing all the letters of the Torah that integrate all life; and this is not the place to elaborate further]
דְּבָעֵינַן שֶׁיּוּכַל לִמְחוֹת
because in this world of free choice and human responsibility, we strictly require that the writing be capable of being erased.
וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן "עַל סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ"
Furthermore, there is an additional way to explain the Talmudic phrasing "fathoming the ultimate end of his mind,"
וְיוּבַן גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ: "שֶׁמֵּאִיר" וְכוּלֵי "שֶׁמַּנְהִיר" וְכוּלֵי
and through this will also be understood what the Gemara states immediately following (Eruvin 13b): "that he illuminates (me'ir)" etc., "that he enlightens (manhir)" etc.
דְּיֵשׁ לְהָבִין: לָמָּה זֶה "מֵאִיר" וְזֶה "מַנְהִיר"?
For one must understand: why does the Talmud employ the Hebrew term me'ir for one Sage, while using the Aramaic term manhir for the other?
וּקְרָאוּהוּ "נְהוֹרַאי", וְלֹא גַּם כֵּן "מֵאִיר", וְהָעִנְיָן לִכְאוֹרָה אֶחָד
And why did they name him Nehorai rather than likewise calling him Me'ir, given that both concepts seemingly express the identical meaning?
גַּם לָמָּה שִׁנּוּ כְּלָל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וַהֲלֹא "נְהוֹרַאי" מוֹרֶה גַּם כֵּן "מַנְהִיר"?
Furthermore, why alter Rabbi Meir's primary name at all, since Nehorai also signifies one who enlightens?
וְעוֹד, אֵיךְ "מֵאִיר בַּהֲלָכָה" וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ?
Moreover, how can it be said that he "illuminates the eyes of the Sages in practical halachah," yet the practical halachic ruling is not established in accordance with his view?
אֲבָל הָעִנְיָן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (דַּף י״ט עַמּוּד א׳): "בַּתְּחִלָּה תּוֹרַת הַשֵּׁם, וּלְבַסּוֹף תּוֹרָתוֹ"
Rather, the matter corresponds to what is taught in Avodah Zarah (19a): "Initially it is called 'the Torah of Hashem,' but ultimately it is called 'his own Torah'";
וְהַיְנוּ תְּחִלַּת הַהַשָּׂגָה, זֶה נִגְלֶה גַּם לַנִּבְרָאִים זוּלָתוֹ
that is, the initial stage of Torah comprehension is accessible and revealed to other human beings as well,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּסּוֹף, כְּשֶׁמַּשִּׂיג הַנֶּעְלָם מִן הַזּוּלַת, זֶה נִקְרָא "תּוֹרָתוֹ", שֶׁאֵין אַחֵר יוֹדְעָהּ וּמַשִּׂיגָהּ מִקּוֹדֶם

whereas at the ultimate stage, when a Sage grasps that transcendent depth which is hidden from all others, it is uniquely designated as "his Torah," for no other person previously perceived or attained it.
וְעִנְיַן "מֵאִיר" וּ"מַנְהִיר" אֶחָד, רַק שֶׁזֶּה לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְזֶה לְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
The conceptual themes of me'ir and manhir share a single root meaning, except that the former is Holy Tongue (Hebrew) while the latter is Aramaic;
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּשַׁבָּת (דַּף י״ב עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁאֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מַכִּירִים בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
and it is well known what the Sages stated in Shabbat (12b): that the ministering angels do not recognize the Aramaic tongue.
וְלָכֵן "מַנְהִיר" רוֹמֵז אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא נֶעְלָם
Therefore, the Aramaic term manhir points to the concealed light of Torah which remains hidden
[וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר עוֹד: "מַנְהִיר" לְשׁוֹן הַמְשָׁכָה כְּמוֹ נְהָרוֹת הַמּוֹשְׁכִין
[and one may further suggest that manhir connotes flowing conveyance (hamshachah), like drawn, flowing rivers (neharot);
וּמִזֶּה "נְהוֹרַאי" שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא רָצָה לוֹמַר הַמְשָׁכָה מִזְּמַן לִזְמַן, שֶׁזּוֹכֵר מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בִּזְמַן קוֹדֵם, וְכֵן הַמְשָׁכָה מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם, וְזֶהוּ הַנֶּעְלָם]

and from this, the Talmudic name Nehorai signifies a continuous transmission across time—remembering that which occurred in earlier epochs—as well as across space, which represents the realm of the concealed],
מַה שֶּׁאֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, שֶׁהֵם הַיּוֹתֵר שְׁלֵמִים בַּנִּגְלוֹת מֵהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם, אֵין מַשִּׂיגִים אוֹתוֹ
which even the ministering angels, consummate as they are in perceiving the manifest revelations of Hashem, cannot comprehend.
שֶׁהַנֶּעְלָם זֶה חֵלֶק אָדָם מֵאֱלֹוקִי לָבוֹא אֶת נֶעְלָמִים, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר

For penetrating the concealed divine realm is man's unique transcendent portion from God, allowing him to commune with hidden mysteries, an ability not granted to the ministering angels, as written elsewhere.
וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, עֶצֶם שְׁמוֹ רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי, עַל הַפְלָגַת נְהִירוּתוֹ שֶׁהִיא בְּנֶעְלָם וְעֹמֶק
Thus, regarding Rabbi Meir, his essential name was truly Rabbi Nehorai, marking the extraordinary intensity of his inner illumination (nehirut) which penetrated the concealed and fathomless depths;
אֲבָל עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים בַּהֲלָכָה הָיָה רַק מֵאִיר בַּנִּגְלֶה
however, with respect to the normative vision of the Sages in halachah, he was merely me'ir—illuminating within the revealed, accessible framework.
אֲבָל עַל "סוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ", שֶׁהוּא הַסּוֹף שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "תּוֹרָתוֹ" וְהַנֶּעְלָם שֶׁנִּגְלָה לוֹ, הָיָה עָמוֹק בְּיוֹתֵר
Yet regarding "the ultimate end of his mind"—that sublime culmination termed "his own Torah," the transcendent realm revealed exclusively to him—it was profoundly deep,
וְלֹא עָמְדוּ עָלָיו חֲבֵרָיו, שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתָם, וְלֹא הִנְהִיר עֵינֵיהֶם בּוֹ
and his colleagues could not fathom it, for it lay far beyond their spiritual capacity, nor could he transmit that concealed illumination to enlighten their eyes.
רַק חָכָם אַחֵר שֶׁקְּרָאוּהוּ "רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי" הִנְהִיר עֵינֵיהֶם בְּנֶעְלָמוֹת שֶׁהָיָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתָם
It was only another Sage [Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh] who was also designated "Rabbi Nehorai" who enlightened their eyes in hidden depths that remained within their attainable level.
[וּבָזֶה יִתְיַשֵּׁב דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּיִחוּד "רִמּוֹן מָצָא" וְכוּלֵי, וְגָמַר מִפּוּמֵיהּ דְּאַחֵר (חֲגִיגָה דַּף ט״ו עַמּוּד ב׳)

[And through this it is resolved why Rabbi Meir specifically was capable of "finding a pomegranate, eating its interior, and discarding its peel," continuing to learn Torah from the mouth of Acher (Elisha ben Avuyah, Chagigah 15b);
שֶׁכְּפִי מַדְרֵגָתוֹ לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ, אֵין חִלּוּק בֵּין צַדִּיק לְרָשָׁע, וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ]

for according to his transcendent vantage point of demonstrating purity even within an impure creeping creature (sheretz), at that primordial root there is no division between righteous and wicked; and this is not the place to elaborate further].
[ח] וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁיָּדַע לְטַהֵר הַשֶּׁרֶץ (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם) — [8]
And this likewise explains the matter of that disciple [in Yavneh] who knew how to demonstrate ritual purity for a creeping creature (sheretz, Eruvin 13b):
שֶׁהוּא כִּנּוּי לְכָל הָעֲבֵרוֹת הַשְּׁכִיחוֹת
which serves as a metaphor for all common, prevalent transgressions,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁלְהֵי יוֹמָא: "טוֹבֵל וְשֶׁרֶץ בְּיָדוֹ", דְּנָקַט "שֶׁרֶץ" שֶׁהוּא הַטֻּמְאָה הַשְּׁכִיחָה

just as stated at the conclusion of Yoma (85b): "one who immerses in a ritual pool while holding a sheretz in his hand," where the Sages chose a sheretz specifically because it represents the most common form of defilement;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁרָגִיל כֵּן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בַּתַּלְמוּד לִתְפֹּס שֶׁרֶץ לְמָשָׁל בְּטֻמְאָה, וְכֵן בְּרֵישׁ כֵּלִים פָּתַח תַּנָּא בּוֹ
as the Talmud is accustomed everywhere to select a sheretz as the prototypical archetype of ritual impurity, and likewise the Tanna opens with it at the beginning of Tractate Keilim.
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר לְטַהֵר כָּל רָשָׁע, דֻּגְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁמְּטַהֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁלְהֵי יוֹמָא (דַּף פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳)

That is to say, his capacity was to demonstrate spiritual purity for every sinner, patterned after Hashem, Blessed be He, Who purifies, as written at the conclusion of Yoma (85b): "[Before Whom do you purify yourselves, and Who purifies you? Your Father in Heaven]";
וְרָצָה לוֹמַר מִצַּד אַחְדוּתוֹ הַפָּשׁוּט הָרָמוּז בְּשֵׁם "הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא" אֵצֶל רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, אֵין מָקוֹם לְטֻמְאָתוֹ

meaning that from the vantage point of His absolute, simple Oneness—alluded to by our Sages of blessed memory in the transcendent title HaKadosh Baruch Hu—there is no place or existence for defilement whatsoever.
וְזֶה הָיְתָה מַדְרֵגַת שִׂכְלוֹ וְהַשָּׂגָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כְּלָל מָקוֹם אֶצְלוֹ לְטֻמְאָה, וְהָיָה טָהוֹר בְּכָל מִינֵי טָהֳרָה

And this was the elevated stature of intellect and perception possessed by that disciple, such that in his perception there was no realm for defilement at all, perceiving all existence as purified through every dimension of purity.
וְהֵם מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים מִקְוֵה טָהֳרָה בַּיָּם שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר לְהַלָּן, שֶׁזֶּה שְׁלֵמוּת הַטָּהֳרָה

And these correspond to the one hundred and fifty measures of ritual pools (mikva'ot) contained within the molten "Sea of Solomon" (in the First Temple), as will be explained further, representing the consummate perfection of purity;
וְזֶהוּ מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים טְעָמִים שֶׁאָמַר לְטָהֳרָתוֹ
and this corresponds to the one hundred and fifty rationales/tastes (ta'amim) he articulated to demonstrate its purity.
וְרָבִינָא בִּקֵּשׁ לְטַהֵר כָּל שֶׁרֶץ מִן הַדִּין [שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַגְּבוּל], וְנִדְחוּ דְּבָרָיו

Ravina, however, sought to declare every sheretz pure based strictly on halachic legal inference (min hadin, which embodies the domain of contraction and bounded judgment), and his argument was refuted,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת מִן הַדִּין טָמֵא
because in absolute halachic reality, from the perspective of judgment it is genuinely impure;
רַק שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים מִינֵי טְעִימוֹת שֶׁל טָהֳרָה לְטוֹעֲמֶיהָ
but there exist one hundred and fifty mystical "tastes" of purity for those who taste them,
אֲשֶׁר חַיִּים הַנִּצְחִיִּים שֶׁל הַשָּׂגַת אַחְדוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַפְּשׁוּטָה גַּם אַחַר בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָמוֹת זָכוּ
who have merited the eternal life of perceiving His simple, primordial Oneness as it persists unbroken even after the creation of the worlds.
וְעִנְיַן דִּבְרֵי רָבִינָא, כִּי נָחָשׁ וְשֶׁרֶץ הֵם שְׁנֵי רָאשֵׁי הַטֻּמְאוֹת שֶׁל "לֹא תִרְצַח" וְ"לֹא תִנְאָף"

The inner meaning of Ravina's reasoning is that the serpent (nachash) and the creeping creature (sheretz) represent the two primary archetypes of defilement corresponding to "Do not murder" and "Do not commit adultery,"
שֶׁהֵם רָאשִׁים לְכָל הָעֲבֵרוֹת וּמִדּוֹת רָעוֹת כִּידוּעַ
which serve as the master roots of all transgressions and corrupt character traits, as is known.
וְיָדוּעַ דִּרְצִיחָה אֵינָהּ מִמִּדַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהַגִּבְעֹנִים לֹא מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל [הֵמָּה]"
And it is known that bloodshed and cruelty are foreign to the innate nature of Israel, as written regarding vengeance: "Now the Gibeonites were not of the Children of Israel";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּמְצֹרָע דְּנִשְׁתַּלַּח חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל (עַיֵּן פְּרִי צַדִּיק חֵלֶק ב׳, לְפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר ה׳, אוֹת ז׳)

and as manifested in the leper (metzora, stricken for malicious speech leading to division), who is expelled entirely outside all three camps of Israel (see Pri Tzaddik, Vol. 2, Parashat Parah, discourse 5, letter 7);
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תַּאֲוָה שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ טֻמְאַת זִיבָה, אֵין מִשְׁתַּלַּח מִמַּחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל

whereas physical lust and desire, whose defilement is embodied by bodily discharge (zivah), is expelled only from the camp of the Divine Presence (Machaneh Shechinah) but not outside the general camp of Israel,
שֶׁזֶּה שַׁיָּךְ וְשָׁכִיחַ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאַף בְּהֶתֵּר שֶׁלּוֹ יֵשׁ טֻמְאָה [כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פֶּרֶק י״ד לְגִרְסַת הֶעָרוּךְ) בֶּעָוֹן מָלֵא]

because physical desire is relevant and common within Israel, and even within its sanctioned expression there can exist traces of defilement [as our Sages noted in Vayikra Rabbah 14 regarding marital intimacy].
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּרְצִיחָה אֵין מָקוֹם לְטֻמְאָה, שֶׁזֶּה חֵלֶק הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת, וּבָהֶם אֵין שַׁיָּךְ כְּלָל שׁוּם טֻמְאָה

In murder, however, there is no conceptual room for ritual defilement (tum'ah), because murder belongs exclusively to the realm of idolatrous nations, and with respect to idolaters the halachic category of ritual impurity does not apply in essence;
[וְאַף מִתַּקָּנַת חֲכָמִים אֵין טֻמְאָתָם כְּטֻמְאַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם נִקְרָאִים מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה
[and even according to Rabbinic decree, their impurity is not identical to that of Israel, for Israel alone possesses the sanctity capable of becoming ritually defiled;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הֵם בְּעֶצֶם וּמִלֵּדָה מִבֶּטֶן עִקַּר הַתְחָלַת הִתְהַוּוּתָן מִיָּד טְמֵאִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר]
whereas idolaters, from the inception of their physical gestation and birth, are categorized as impure by their very status, as I have written elsewhere],
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל טֻמְאָה וּמַרְבִּים טֻמְאָה בָּעוֹלָם
even though they serve as the root of cosmic impurity and proliferate defilement throughout the world,
כְּמוֹ דְּאֵין שַׁיָּכִים כָּל הָעֲבֵרוֹת בָּהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵם שֹׁרֶשׁ לְכָל הָעֲבֵרוֹת
just as the formal system of Torah transgressions does not apply to them, even though they represent the source of all sins;
כִּי לֹא שַׁיָּךְ טֻמְאָה אֶלָּא בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ שַׁיָּכוּת לְטָהֳרָה
for ritual defilement exists solely where there is an innate receptivity and connection to holiness and purity.
וְזֶה קַל וָחֹמֶר דְּרָבִינָא מִנָּחָשׁ לְשֶׁרֶץ
And this explains Ravina's logical deduction (a fortiori / kal vachomer) from the serpent (nachash, which kills and represents murder) to the creeping creature (sheretz, which represents desire):
לְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַרְבֶּה טֻמְאָה וְנוֹפוֹ נוֹטֶה לִמְקוֹם טָהֳרָה, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מָקוֹם לְטֻמְאָה

if the deadly serpent does not impart ritual defilement, then regarding a sheretz, which does not kill and whose ultimate branch leans toward a place of purity, all the more so should the greater measure of goodness prevail so that it imparts no defilement;
וְאִם עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אֵין נֶעֱנָשִׁים עַל שֶׁעוֹבְרִים עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן יִשְׂרָאֵל
and if the idolaters are not held accountable for violating the specific commandments of the Torah, all the more so should Israel be defended.
וְזֶה קַל וָחֹמֶר פְּרִיכָא כִּדְדָחֵי
Yet this kal vachomer is flawed and refutable, as the Gemara readily knocked it down:
דְּהָתָם מַעֲשֵׂה קוֹץ בְּלִי דַּעַת עָבֵיד, "וּבְלִיַּעַל כְּקוֹץ מֻנָד כֻּלָּהַם"
for there, the serpent acts mindlessly like a mindless thorn, and Scripture states: "the base scoundrels are all like thorns driven away";
וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ טֻמְאָה אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת, וְלֹא בְּאוֹתָם שֶׁ"נִמְשְׁלוּ כַּבְּהֵמוֹת נִדְמוּ"
for the spiritual reality of defilement applies solely to one endowed with divine consciousness (Da'at), and not to those who "are compared to the beasts that perish."
וְאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם): "תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר" וְכוּלֵי
And the Gemara related there (Eruvin 13b): "Rabbi Meir had a certain disciple [who articulated forty-eight reasons to declare the creeping creature pure]":
שֶׁאַל תַּחְשֹׁב שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה וּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְתַלְמִיד דְּיַבְנֶה סוֹתֵר מַדְרֵגַת הַהַגְדָּרָה
so that you should not imagine that this transcendent level of Rabbi Meir and the disciple in Yavneh contradicts the reality of bounded halachic structure;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַכֹּל מִמַּעְיָנוֹ נוֹבֵעַ
for in truth, the structured framework itself flows directly from his transcendent wellspring.
וְלָכֵן אָמַר שֶׁתַּלְמִידוֹ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁנָּבַע מִמַּעְיָנוֹ, הָיָה אוֹמֵר אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה טְעָמִים — מִן אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה מִינֵי טְעִימוֹת
Therefore it states that the disciple of Rabbi Meir, who drew from his master's wellspring, stated forty-eight reasons—reflecting forty-eight distinct tastes/sensations of wisdom
[כַּאֲשֶׁר חֵךְ אֹכֶל יִטְעַם, כֵּן הַרְגָּשַׁת הַלֵּב בְּכָל דְּבַר אֱמֶת וְצֶדֶק, כְּעִנְיַן "טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ כִּי טוֹב הַשֵּׁם"]
[just as the palate tastes food, so does the heart spiritually taste every matter of truth and righteousness, in the sense of "taste and see that Hashem is good"],
כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִקְנֵית
corresponding to the forty-eight qualities through which the Torah is acquired (Avot 6:6);
עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶצְלוֹ בְּקִנְיָן גָּמוּר, צָרִיךְ אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים
for in order for the words of Torah to become fully integrated within a person as an enduring acquisition, forty-eight attributes are required.
וּמִסְּתָמָא אֵינָם בְּפַעַם אַחַת רַק לְאַט לְאַט, וְהֵם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה מַדְרֵגוֹת
These acquisitions self-evidently do not occur all at once but step by step, constituting forty-eight ascending rungs;
וּבְכָל מַדְרֵגָה הוּא מַרְגִּישׁ תּוֹסֶפֶת קִנְיַן הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶצְלוֹ וְטַעַם מְחֻדֶּשֶׁת בְּהַרְגָּשָׁה מְחֻדֶּשֶׁת כְּפִי מַדְרֵגַת הַדָּבָר הַהוּא
and upon each rung he experiences an added integration of the words of Torah and a renewed taste through refined spiritual feeling matching that level,
עַד שֶׁהִשְׁלִים כָּל אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה דָּבָר, וְהָיָה דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֶצְלוֹ בְּקִנְיָן, וְטָעַם כָּל הָאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה מִינֵי טְעִימוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הֲלָכָה וַהֲלָכָה
until he mastered all forty-eight qualities, fully acquiring the Torah and tasting all forty-eight spiritual dimensions within each and every halachah.
וְזֶה הָיָה כְּפִי הֲלָכָה הַמּוּגְבֶּלֶת: עַל טָהוֹר טָהוֹר, וְעַל טָמֵא טָמֵא
And this discernment operated within the defined boundaries of practical halachah: declaring the pure to be pure, and the impure to be impure;
וְזֶה תַּלְמִיד שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁלָּמַד וְקִבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ מַדְרֵגָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר, כִּי הַכֹּל אֶחָד וְזֶה יוֹצֵא מִזֶּה

and this student of Rabbi Meir, who absorbed and received from him his spiritual stature, demonstrated that both levels are one, the bounded discipline emerging organically from the transcendent source.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ: "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, וַהֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל"

And this explains why the heavenly voice (Bat Kol) declared immediately thereafter (Eruvin 13b): "These and those are the words of the Living God, yet the practical halachah is according to Beit Hillel":
"אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" הוּא מַדְרֵגַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר
"these and those are the words of the Living God" represents the transcendent vantage point of Rabbi Meir,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּבְרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק א׳, הֲלָכָה ה׳) עַל "וַהשֵּׁם אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת" — לָמָּה? שֶׁהוּא אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
as taught in the Jerusalem Talmud (Berakhot 1:5) on the verse, "And Hashem God is Truth"—why? Because He is the "Living God";
וְיָדוּעַ "אֱמֶת" הוּא שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה
and it is known that "Truth" (Emet) corresponds to the Name Havayah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ״א) דֶּאֱמֶת רֹאשׁ וְסוֹף וְאֶמְצָעִי שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם אוֹתִיּוֹת
and as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 81), the letters of Emet form the beginning, middle, and end of the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet;
וְכֵן פֵּרוּשׁ שֵׁם הַוָּיָ״ה: "הָיָה, הֹוֶה, וְיִהְיֶה" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטּוּר אֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן ה׳)
and likewise the essential definition of the Name Havayah is "He was, He is, and He will be" (as codified in Tur, Orach Chaim 5).
וְהַטַּעַם הוּא שֶׁהוּא אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים
And the reason for this is that He is the "Living God,"
וְ"חַיִּים" רָצָה לוֹמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ הֶפְסֵק לְעוֹלָם וְאֵין לוֹ גְּבוּל
where "Life" signifies reality that possesses no cessation whatsoever and is bounded by no limit.
וְזֶהוּ "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים", דְּדִבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת "וַהשֵּׁם אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת", שָׁם הוּא כְּדִבְרֵי אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ, שֶׁאֵין גָּדֵר וּגְבוּל

And this is "these and those are the words of the Living God": within the transcendent plane of the "Living God"—which is the level of "Hashem God is Truth"—both opposing positions are simultaneously valid, for at that primordial source there are no rigid fences or finite borders.
אֲבָל הַהֲלָכָה, שֶׁהִיא הַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם, הִיא כְּבֵית הִלֵּל, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מִתְנַהֵג בִּגְבוּל

However, practical halachah, which governs actual conduct within this physical world, follows Beit Hillel, because, as established above, the present world was purposefully created to be governed within the framework of boundary and measure.
שָׁם (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים נֶחְלְקוּ" וְכוּלֵי
There (Eruvin 13b): "For three years [Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel] disputed," etc.;
פֵּרוּשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים הוּא שָׁלֹשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת דְּחָשֵׁיב לְהַלָּן, שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת: אַבְרָהָם, יִצְחָק, וְיַעֲקֹב
the meaning of "three years" corresponds to three spiritual levels enumerated below, which align with the three Patriarchs: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
הַמַּקְבִּילִים נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינֵי רָע, שֶׁלְּעֻמָּתָן שָׁלֹשׁ אֻמּוֹת: אֱדוֹם, וּמוֹאָב, וְעַמּוֹן
which stand parallel against three primary modes of evil, mirrored oppositely by three nations: Edom, Moab, and Ammon.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשׁ הַמִּדּוֹת רָעוֹת: כַּעַס
As I have heard, these embody three master character flaws: anger
[אֱדוֹם שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד "לֹא תִרְצַח", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף קצ״ב עַמּוּד ב׳), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה"
[Edom, which opposes "Do not murder," as our Sages of blessed memory noted (Zohar Vol. III, 192b), and as written: "By your sword shall you live";
וּמִמֶּנּוּ לֹא נִשְׁתְּלָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה תִּקּוּנוֹ עַל יָדוֹ כִּידוּעַ
and from Edom the Davidic dynasty was not planted, for its rectification could not emerge through it, as is known.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְנוּ דְּכַעַס אֵינוֹ מִמַּחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד רוֹמֵז לִכְלָלוּת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּידוּעַ, כִּי הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא הָעָם
And as we wrote, anger has no place within the camp of Israel, and the Davidic monarchy symbolizes the totality of Knesset Yisrael, as is known, for the king embodies the people;
אֲבָל מַפַּלְתָּם עַל יְדֵי בֵּית יוֹסֵף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא דַּף קכ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳), כִּי הוּא הֵפֶךְ הַכַּעַס כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
but their downfall occurs through the house of Joseph, as our Sages stated (Bava Batra 123b), because Joseph is the antithesis of anger, as written elsewhere;
וְאֵין שְׁתִילַת הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמַּחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל מִזֶּה, וּכְמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּיבָמוֹת (דַּף ע״ט עַמּוּד א׳): "שְׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים" וְכוּלֵי

and no roots of Knesset Yisrael within the camp of Israel sprout from this, matching what our Sages said in Yevamot (79a): "There are three signs [of the Jewish nation: merciful, bashful, and performers of lovingkindness],"
שֶׁהֵם כֻּלָּם נֶגֶד עֵשָׂו, שֶׁרוֹמֵז בִּשְׁלֹשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹתָיו הֵפֶךְ זֶה
which all stand directly against Esau, whose three Hebrew letters allude to the exact opposite of these three;
וְהֵם שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים שֶׁנִּזְכַּר מְחִיָּתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִלָּה דַּף ז׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ]
and these mirror the three times the obliteration of Amalek/Esau is mentioned in Scripture (Megillah 7a); and this is not the place to elaborate],
וְגַאֲוָה
and arrogance
[מוֹאָב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שָׁמַעְנוּ גְאוֹן מוֹאָב גֵּא מְאֹד" וְגוֹמֵר
[Moab, as written: "We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is exceedingly proud," etc.;
וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִשְׁתַּל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְתִקּוּנוֹ דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁאָמַר: "וְאָנֹכִי תוֹלַעַת", וּמַשְׁפִּיל עַצְמוֹ עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ]

and from Moab roots were grafted into Israel [via Ruth], whose spiritual rectification was King David, peace be upon him, who declared: "Yet I am a worm," humbling himself completely for the honor of his Creator],
וְשֶׁקֶר
and falsehood
[עַמּוֹן, וּלְכָךְ קְרָאַתּוּ "בֶּן עַמִּי", שֶׁהוּא הַעֲלָמַת הָאֱמֶת
[Ammon, which is why Lot's younger daughter named him Ben-Ammi ("son of my kinsman"), which concealed the incestuous truth;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נָזִיר דַּף כ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁקִּבְּלָה שָׂכָר עַל זֶה
nonetheless, our Sages stated (Nazir 23b) that she received a reward for this modesty of language,
כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁקֶר טוֹב, וּבְגִין דָּא מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹת (עַיֵּן בָּבָא מְצִיעָא דַּף כ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳)
for there exists constructive deviation from the truth for peace and humility, for which reason it is permitted to alter facts in certain matters (see Bava Metzia 23b);
וְגַם שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִצַּד בְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם, דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא "עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא" (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פֶּרֶק כ״ו) שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֵּן
and this stems from the cosmic design of Creation, which is why this realm is termed the "world of falsehood" (alma d'shikra, Vayikra Rabbah 26), as all of this physical world functions this way.
וּלְפִיכָךְ לֹא נִשְׁתַּלָּה עַד רְחַבְעָם, שֶׁהוּא אַחַר בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְמָשִׁיחַ

Consequently, Ammon was not grafted into the royal line until Rehoboam [via Naamah the Ammonitess], which occurred after the building of the Temple and King Solomon, peace be upon him, who alludes to Mashiach;
אַחַר כָּךְ הוּא זְבִיחַת הַיֵּצֶר לְגַמְרֵי, וְאָז נִסְתַּלֵּק עָלְמָא דְּשִׁקְרָא
for thereafter comes the total slaughter of the evil inclination, whereupon the world of falsehood is utterly dissolved,
וּרְחַבְעָם תִּקּוּנוֹ, לָכֵן אָחַז בֶּאֱמֶת וְעָזַב עֲצַת הַזְּקֵנִים]
and Rehoboam was its rectification, which is why he spoke unvarnished harsh truth and abandoned the diplomatic counsel of the elders].
וְשָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת אֵלּוּ לֹא נִתְקְנוּ עֲדַיִן לְגַמְרֵי עַד עֵת קֵץ
And these three flawed traits have not yet been fully rectified until the End of Days;
לָכֵן לֹא זָכוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָז לִנְחֹל שָׁלֹשׁ אֻמּוֹת אֵלּוּ
therefore, the Children of Israel did not merit then [in antiquity] to inherit the territories of these three nations [Edom, Moab, and Ammon],
וְלֶעָתִיד יִזְכּוּ גַּם לָהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פֶּרֶק מ״ד]
but in the Messianic Future they will merit them as well, as our Sages stated (Bereishit Rabbah 44),
וְלֹא יִתְעַסְּקוּ עוֹד בִּסְבִיבַת הָהָר [כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סֻכָּה דַּף נ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "הַצַּדִּיקִים נִדְמֶה לָהֶם כְּהַר"]
and they will no longer struggle in circling the mountain [as written in Sukkah 52a: "To the righteous, the evil inclination appears like an insurmountable mountain"].
וְהִנֵּה אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין דַּף צ״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "וַהשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ — שֶׁהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ"
Behold, our Sages stated (Sanhedrin 93b): "'And Hashem is with him' [said of David]—this teaches that the halachah is established in accordance with his view";
שֶׁלְּכַוֵּן הֲלָכָה לַאֲמִתָּהּ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּקִרְבּוֹ קָדוֹשׁ וַהשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, בְּלִי שׁוּם נְגִיעָה לְגוּפוֹ כְּלָל
for to determine halachah to its absolute divine truth, one must be inwardly holy with Hashem truly with him, entirely free of personal bias or physical self-interest;
אָז יוּכַל לְכַוֵּן אֲמִתַּת הֲלָכָה
only then can one arrive at the unadulterated truth of the halachah.
וְהוּא מַדְרֵגַת הִלֵּל שֶׁאָמַר: "בָּרוּךְ הַשֵּׁם יוֹם יוֹם" וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבֵיצָה (דַּף ט״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
And this was the spiritual level of Hillel, who declared: "Blessed be Hashem day by day," etc., as recorded in Beitzah (16a),
וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ל״ד) דַּאֲזַל לְמִגְמַל חֶסֶד עִם הָדָא עֲלוּבְתָא, שֶׁמַּמָּשׁ כְּזָר נֶחְשְׁבוּ לוֹ

and in Vayikra Rabbah (34), where he said he was going to perform an act of kindness for "this poor guest" (referring to his own physical body), which he regarded with total detachment as if it were an outsider;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שַׁמַּאי הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהַכְנִיס קְדֻשָּׁה בְּכָל דְּבַר מַאֲכָל שֶׁאָכַל בְּכָל יוֹם עַל יְדֵי כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת
whereas Shammai felt the need to consciously inject holiness into each food item he ate daily by designating it for the honor of Shabbat,
וְלֹא נֶחְשַׁב בְּעֵינָיו הָאֲכִילָה קְדֻשָּׁה כִּגְמִילַת חֶסֶד
for in his eyes bodily eating was not inherently sanctified merely as an act of altruistic benevolence.
וְהַבֵּרוּר עַל "וַהשֵּׁם עִמּוֹ" הִיא נְקִיּוּת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשֵׁי מִדּוֹת אֵלּוּ
And the confirmation of "Hashem is with him" consists of absolute purity within these three master character traits,
שֶׁהַמִּדּוֹת רָעוֹת כֻּלָּם הוּא מִצַּד הַחֹמֶר וְהַנְּגִיעָה לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ
for all negative character traits stem from material coarseness and self-interested seeking of personal gratification.
וְזֶהוּ הַוִּכּוּחַ שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה רוֹמֵז עַל הֶקֵּף סֵדֶר שָׁלֵם
And this explains their three-year debate, where "three years" in the teachings of our Sages alludes to the traversal of a complete, comprehensive cycle,
כְּמוֹ הַשָּׁנָה הַמַּקֶּפֶת סֵדֶר שָׁלֵם, כִּידוּעַ לְשׁוֹן "שָׁנָה" עַל שֵׁם "מִשְׁנֶה", שֶׁחוֹזֵר וְשׁוֹנֶה סֵדֶר אַחֵר עַל כָּל מִדָּה
just as a solar year traverses a complete seasonal cycle (the word shanah [year] deriving from mishneh [repetition], as it cycles through a complete review of each spiritual trait);
הִשְׁלִימוּ הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם בְּכָל חֲלָקֶיהָ וּפְרָטֶיהָ עִיּוּן גָּמוּר
they completed a thorough analytical review through every facet and sub-detail,
עַד שֶׁלְּסוֹף שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים נִתְבָּרֵר הַבַּת קוֹל, וּמִן הַשָּׁמַיִם הוֹכִיחַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם עִם בֵּית הִלֵּל וַהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתָן
until at the conclusion of three years, the heavenly voice (Bat Kol) issued forth, proving from Heaven that Hashem was with Beit Hillel and that the halachah follows their view
[וְרוֹמֵז בַּת קוֹל, שֶׁשֵּׂכֶל הָאָדָם נִלְאָה לְהַשִּׂיג אֲמִתִּיַּת הַמַּדְרֵגָה לוּלֵי עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֵאמֹר: "זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ, לְכוּ בָהּ", רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה הָאֱמֶת]

[and the Bat Kol signifies that mortal human intellect tires of grasping the absolute truth of this stature without divine assistance declaring: "This is the way, walk in it," meaning that this represents the living truth].
"לְפִי שֶׁנּוֹחִין" הָיָה — זֶהוּ הֶעְדֵּר כַּעַס
"Because they were pleasant/patient"—this represents the total absence of anger;
"וַעֲלוּבִין" — הֶעְדֵּר גַּאֲוָה
"and self-effacing/modest"—this represents the absence of arrogance;
"וְשׁוֹנִין דִּבְרֵיהֶם וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי", וְאֵין מַעֲלִימִין דִּבְרֵי שֶׁכְּנֶגְדָּן כְּדֶרֶךְ הֶחָפֵץ בְּנִצּוּחַ — זֶהוּ הֶעְדֵּר הַשֶּׁקֶר
"and they taught their own words alongside the words of Beit Shammai," never concealing the opposing view as contentious debaters do—this represents the absence of falsehood;
"וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא [שֶׁמַּקְדִּימִין דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְדִבְרֵיהֶם]" — הִיא הַשְּׁלֵמוּת הַגָּמוּר הַקַּיָּם לָעַד
"and not only that, [but they gave precedence to the words of Beit Shammai before their own]"—this represents consummate, enduring perfection,
כְּמִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, "חַי וְקַיָּם" לָעַד (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה דַּף כ״ה עַמּוּד א׳)
matching the attribute of King David, peace be upon him, who "lives and endures" forever (Rosh Hashanah 25a).
כִּי אֵלּוּ נֶגֶד שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל: אַבְרָהָם אִישׁ חֶסֶד — הֵפֶךְ כַּעַס
For these three traits correspond to the three Patriarchs, as I wrote above: Abraham, the man of lovingkindness (Chesed), is the antithesis of anger;
וְיִצְחָק יִרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּהַקְדָּמַת הַזֹּהַר (דַּף י״א עַמּוּד ב׳): "בְּיִרְאָתְךָ" — דָּא יִצְחָק (עַל פִּי הַגִּרְסָה בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳, עַיֵּן שָׁם)
and Isaac embodies awe/reverence (Gevurah), as written in the Introduction to the Zohar (11b): "'In Your awe'—this is Isaac,"
הֵפֶךְ גַּאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי דְּעִקַּר יִרְאָה הַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עֵקֶב עֲנָוָה יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם"
which is the antithesis of pride, for as I have heard, the essence of awe is recognizing one's own deficiency, as written: "The heel of humility is the fear of Hashem";
וֶ"אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" — הֵפֶךְ שֶׁקֶר
and "Truth unto Jacob" (Tiferet) is the antithesis of falsehood.
וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, רֶגֶל רְבִיעִי שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה, מִדָּתוֹ שָׁלוֹם, הֵפֶךְ מַחֲלֹקֶת וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע, שֶׁהֵם בַּעֲלֵי רִיב דָּוִד

And King David, peace be upon him, the fourth foot of the Supernal Chariot (Merkavah), embodies the attribute of Peace (Shalom / Malchut), the antithesis of discord and slander, which characterized David's adversaries;
כִּי מַלְכוּת הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַיִּקְרָא לוֹ" וְגוֹמֵר "שַׂר שָׁלוֹם"
for true Kingship is designed to establish peace in the world, as written: "And his name shall be called... Prince of Peace."
וְאָמְרוּ (יְבָמוֹת דַּף ס״ה עַמּוּד ב׳, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה סוֹף פֶּרֶק ט׳): גָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם וְכוּלֵי, וְאֵין הַגָּלֻיּוֹת מִתְקַבְּצוֹת וְכוּלֵי
And the Sages stated (Yevamot 65b; Vayikra Rabbah end of ch. 9): Great is peace, etc., and the exiles will not be regathered except through peace,
וְכָל הַתְּפִלּוֹת וּבְרָכוֹת חוֹתְמִין בּוֹ, שֶׁזֶּה הָאַחֲרִית שֶׁל כָּל הַשְּׁלֵמוּת וְהָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁבְּמֶרְכֶּבֶת שְׁלֵמוּת הַבְּרִיאָה
and all liturgical prayers and blessings conclude with peace, for this is the ultimate summit of all spiritual perfection and the final anchor in the chariot of Creation's completeness.
וְהֵם אַרְבַּעַת הַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ח׳) בִּשְׁעַת בְּרִיאָה
And these correspond to the four ministering forces mentioned by our Sages (Bereishit Rabbah ch. 8) at the hour of Man's creation:
חֶסֶד וְצֶדֶק, שֶׁהֵם טוֹב לַבְּרִיּוֹת וְטוֹב לַשָּׁמַיִם, וְהֵם מִדּוֹת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, וְאוֹמְרִים "יִבָּרֵא", שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ טוֹב

Chesed (Lovingkindness) and Tzedek (Righteousness), which are benevolent toward creatures and devout toward Heaven—the attributes of Abraham and Isaac—declared: "Let him be created, for he does acts of kindness";
וְהַפְּסֹלֶת יָצָא בְּיִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו, כְּדֵי שֶׁהַנִּשְׁאָר יִהְיֶה כֻּלּוֹ זַךְ וְנָקִי
and their dross was externalized and expelled into Ishmael and Esau, so that the lineage remaining within Israel was wholly pure and refined.
וֶ"אֱמֶת" וְ"שָׁלוֹם" אוֹמְרִים "אַל יִבָּרֵא", שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ בְּהֵפֶךְ
Emet (Truth) and Shalom (Peace), however, argued: "Let him not be created, for he is full of lies and strife,"
כִּי לֹא נִבְדַּל הַפְּסֹלֶת מֵהֶם, וְגַם הַפְּסֹלֶת בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנֶּה, וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּלַּח חוּץ מִמַּחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל
because regarding them the dross was not cleanly severed and cast outside, for even the sinners among them are still designated with the name of Israel, never being cast outside the camp of Israel.
וְ"הִשְׁלִיךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה" — זֶהוּ יַעֲקֹב רֹאשׁ הָאֻמָּה
And "He cast Truth to the earth"—this is Jacob, the bedrock of the nation;
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ "אֱמֶת" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דַּף ד׳ עַמּוּד ב׳), וְהִיא מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח
and this unfolds through the Torah, concerning which it is written "truth" (Avodah Zarah 4b), which "springs forth from the earth."
וְעַל יָדוֹ יִהְיֶה בֵּרוּר הַשָּׁלֵם, וְיַגִּיעוּ לְאַחֲרִית שְׁלֵמוּת הָאֻמָּה בִּימֵי מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁיָּבוֹא לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם
And through him the absolute clarification will be realized, leading to the ultimate spiritual fruition of the nation in the days of Mashiach, who will come to establish universal peace;
וְעַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ: "וְכָל נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם"
and through the agency of the Torah, regarding which it is written: "And all its paths are peace."
הַנְּתִיבוֹת הֵם הַדְּרָכִים הַצָּרִים, הַיְדוּעִים רַק לִשְׂרִידִים אֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם קוֹרֵא
These "paths" (netivot) are the subtle, narrow pathways known exclusively to the remnant whom Hashem calls.
וְזֶהוּ "וְלֹא עוֹד" וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁזֶּהוּ תֹּקֶף הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם

And this is the inner meaning of "and not only that [did they recite the opposing view, but they gave precedence to the words of Beit Shammai before their own]," which demonstrates the immense power of peace between them;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (דַּף י״ד עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל זֶה: "הָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם [אֱהָבוּ]"
and as applied in Yevamot (14b) to this very dynamic: "[Love] truth and peace"

[זֶה תָּלוּי בָּזֶה: זֶה רִאשׁוֹן וְזֶה אַחֲרוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין דַּף ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "אֶת וָהֵב בְּסוּפָה" — הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא בַּסּוֹף וּבְאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים

[for they depend upon one another: Truth is first and Peace is the ultimate culmination as stated above, matching what our Sages said in Kiddushin 30b on the verse et vahev b'sufah, that authentic peace emerges at the end and in the End of Days;
אֲבָל נִמְשָׁךְ מִמֵּילָא מִן הָאֱמֶת, אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הֶמְשֵׁךְ זְמַן עַד לַסּוֹף לָזֶה]
yet peace flows organically from truth, requiring only an unfolding progression of time to reach that culmination],
שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹהֲגִין אַהֲבָה וְאַחֲוָה זֶה עִם זֶה, לְהַקְדִּים דִּבְרֵי חַבְרֵיהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַלָּלוּ מְטַהֲרִין וְהַלָּלוּ מְטַמְּאִין
that they conducted themselves with genuine love and brotherhood toward one another, giving precedence to their colleagues' statements despite these declaring pure while those declared impure.
וּבֵרוּר זֶה הָיָה בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַּסֻּכָּה וְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ תּוֹךְ הַבַּיִת (סֻכָּה דַּף כ״ח עַמּוּד א׳)

And this clarification occurred specifically in their halachic dispute concerning one whose head and majority of body are within the sukkah while his dining table remains inside the house (Sukkah 28a):
כִּידוּעַ דְּסֻכָּה הוּא הַבִּטָּחוֹן הַגָּמוּר וְהַחִסָּיוֹן בְּצֵל הַשֵּׁם הַסּוֹכֵךְ עָלָיו, וְשֶׁאֵין בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ כְּלוּם, רַק הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם
for as is known, the sukkah embodies consummate trust and sheltering in the protective shadow of Hashem, where man owns nothing and everything is in the hands of Heaven;
וְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ הוּא קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים תּוֹךְ הַבַּיִת, זֶהוּ כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ל״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם"
while his table represents bodily sustenance inside the domestic house, evocative of the rabbinic dictum (Berakhot 33b): "Except for the fear of Heaven,"
דְּקִיּוּם הַחַיִּים נוֹתֵן הַבְּחִירָה בְּיַד הָאָדָם
since sustaining physical life places active free-willed choice into human hands.
אֲבָל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים דְּבֶאֱמֶת הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם
Beit Shammai, however, maintain that in absolute truth everything is in the hands of Heaven;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בָּזֶה, דְּגַם כְּפִי הַנִּרְאֶה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא אֱמֶת דְּחוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
and as I heard regarding this, even though from the outward appearance of this world it is true that free choice governs "except for the fear of Heaven,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא זוֹ הַדֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן אוֹר הַבּוֹטֵחַ בְּשֵׁם הַשֵּׁם בֶּאֱמֶת
nevertheless, this is not the path wherein dwells the transcendent light of one who trusts in the Name of Hashem in ultimate truth;
"וְלֹא קִיַּמְתָּ מִצְוַת סֻכָּה מִיָּמֶיךָ" אִם נָהַגְתָּ כֵּן
and "you have never truly fulfilled the mitzvah of sukkah in your days" if you acted this way [dividing your sustenance from total divine shelter].
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם הַיֵּצֶר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּעִנְיַן "וְאַתָּה הֲסִבֹּתָ" וְגוֹמֵר (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ל״ב עַמּוּד א׳)
For in ultimate truth, even the evil inclination is ordained by Hashem, as expressed in the verse: "And You turned their heart backward" (Berakhot 32a);
וְלֶעָתִיד שֶׁיְּבֹעַר הַיֵּצֶר יִתְבָּרְרוּ דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
and in the Messianic Future when the yetzer hara is purged, the position of Beit Shammai will be vindicated as the operative reality.
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא בֶּן דָּוִד לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, "וְגָר זְאֵב עִם [כֶּבֶשׂ]" וְגוֹמֵר
This will occur when the Son of David arrives to establish universal peace, and "the wolf shall dwell with [the lamb]," etc.;

כִּי עִקַּר הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבֵּין בְּנֵי אָדָם נִמְשָׁךְ [מִצַּד הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁבְּדִבְרֵי הֲלָכָה שֶׁהוּא] מִצַּד הִתְחַלְּקוּת הַגְּבוּלִים שֶׁל הַנִּבְרָאִים, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד גְּבוּל נִפְרָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
for the primary source of dispute among people stems [from halachic controversy, which reflects] the divided boundaries of created beings, where each entity occupies a separate, defined perimeter.

אֲבָל מִצַּד הַבֵּרוּר הַגָּמוּר שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, אָז יִהְיֶה מַדְרֵגַת "אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים" [שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל], וְאֵין מָקוֹם לְמַחֲלֹקֶת

But from the perspective of the consummate realization that all is in the hands of Heaven, the reality of "these and those are the words of the Living God" will reign [which is the transcendent level of Rabbi Meir, as noted above], leaving no room for discord.
אֲבָל עַכְשָׁו [לֹא נִקְבַּע הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וְכֵן] הֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל
But at present [halachah is not established according to Rabbi Meir, as stated above, and likewise] the halachah follows Beit Hillel;
וְנִמְצָא עִנְיַן מַחֲלֹקֶת זוֹ דְּסֻכָּה, אַדְּרַבָּא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אָחֲזוּ בְּמִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָאֲמִתִּית, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים לְהֵפֶךְ
thus regarding this dispute of the sukkah, on the contrary, Beit Shammai held fast to the absolute, essential attribute of King David, peace be upon him, while Beit Hillel held the opposite.

וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכֵי בְּכָאן הָיָה הַבֵּרוּר הַגָּמוּר [דַּוְקָא, וְכָךְ הִיא הַמִּדָּה], שֶׁזֶּהוּ רַק מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים כְּפִי הַהֲלָכָה הָרְאוּיִם לְהִלּוּךְ וְהַנְהָגַת הָעוֹלָם

Even so, precisely here occurred the complete clarification [as is the spiritual dynamic]: that Beit Hillel argued from the viewpoint of practical wisdom, ruling according to the halachic standards appropriate for human conduct in this world;
אֲבָל נְקֻדַּת חַיִּים שֶׁבְּלִבָּם הָיָה דָּבוּק בְּשָׁלוֹם מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בֶּאֱמֶת
yet the innermost vital point of their hearts was genuinely bound to the peace of King David's attribute.

וּבוֹ, בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם דַּוְקָא, נִתְבָּרְרוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁאָחֲזוּ בְּשָׁלוֹם מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְהִקְדִּימוּ דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְדִבְרֵיהֶם, וְהָבֵן זֶה הֵיטֵב

And precisely in that exact context, their integrity was validated as clinging to the peace of King David's trait, in that they gave precedence to the words of Beit Shammai before their own; understand this well.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַחֲלֹקֶת "אִם טוֹב יוֹתֵר שֶׁנִּבְרָא" (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם)
And this is the theme of their dispute whether "it would have been better for man had he been created" (Eruvin 13b):
כִּי עִנְיַן "נִבְרָא" שֶׁהוּא נִפְרָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְנִכָּר לַנִּבְרָא שֶׁהוּא דָּבָר אַחֵר וְחָלוּק מִן הַבּוֹרֵא שֶׁהוּא הַמְּיַחֵד הַכֹּל
for the state of being "created" implies existing as an independent entity, where the creature perceives itself as distinct and separate from the Creator Who unifies all;
וְעִנְיַן "שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא" הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַכֹּל בִּמְקוֹרוֹ [וּכְשֶׁחוֹזֵר לִמְקוֹרוֹ הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא]
while the state of "not having been created" means that all remains rooted in its primal Source [and when returning to its Source, it is as though it was never created as a separate being].
וּשְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת אֱמֶת, וְכַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וַחֲכָמִים
Both levels are true, corresponding, as noted above, to the perspectives of Rabbi Meir and the Sages;
וְזֶה עַצְמוֹ עִנְיַן "קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ" הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל לְמַעְלָה רֹאשׁ, יְעֻיַּן שָׁם בִּדְבָרֵינוּ
and this is the very concept of "the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Shechinah" mentioned above at the beginning, see our words there
[וְזֶהוּ יְסוֹד מַסֶּכֶת עֵירוּבִין, שֶׁיְּסוֹדָהּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד, וְכָל הֲלָכוֹתֶיהָ לְבָרֵר דָּבָר זֶה בָּאוּ]
[and this is the foundation of Tractate Eruvin, whose goal is to transform the public domain into the private domain of the One, and all its laws come to elucidate this principle].
וְחָקְרוּ אֵיזֶה טוֹב יוֹתֵר, וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ הַמַּחֲלֹקֶת דְּשֻׁלְחָנוֹ תּוֹךְ הַבַּיִת אִם יָצְאוּ יְדֵי סֻכָּה
And they analyzed which is better, which is identical to the dispute regarding one whose table is inside the house as to whether he fulfilled the sukkah.
וּלְשׁוֹן "אֵיזֶה נוֹחַ יוֹתֵר" רָצָה לוֹמַר: מִמַּה יֵּשׁ נַחַת לָאָדָם יוֹתֵר
The expression "which is more comfortable/tranquil (no'ach)" asks: from which state does man experience greater spiritual satisfaction and rest:

אִם הַנִּיחָא הִיא מִמַּדְרֵגַת "שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא", שֶׁיָּשִׂים אֶל לִבּוֹ "מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ" בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם עַכְשָׁו כְּעַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, בְּאֵין חוֹצֵץ מְאוּמָה, וּמִזֶּה הוּא הַנִּיחָא הַגְּמוּרָה לָאָדָם [בֶּאֱמֶת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּךְ נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ]

whether rest stems from the level of "not having been created," internalizing that "the whole earth is full of His glory" in absolute truth even now just as before Creation without any barrier, which yields complete tranquility for man [in truth, as they concluded upon voting];
אוֹ אַדְּרַבָּא, הַנִּיחָא הוּא כַּאֲשֶׁר הַבְּחִירָה בְּיָדוֹ וְהוּא בּוֹחֵר חַיִּים
or conversely, whether satisfaction is found when free choice is in his hands and he actively chooses life.
וְעִנְיַן שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בָּזֶה שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה
And the reason they debated this for two and a half years:

כִּי אִיתָא בְּשַׁבָּת (דַּף פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): כָּל זְמַן עַבְדוּת הָאָדָם שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה, עַיֵּן שָׁם הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן, שֶׁבָּהֶם יֵשׁ מָקוֹם לַחֲטֹא וּבָהֶם צָרִיךְ יְגִיעָה לְנַצֵּחַ

for it is taught in Shabbat 89b that the total span of man's active accountability in sin and struggle amounts to twelve and a half years (see the calculation there), during which sin is possible and exertion is required to overcome it,
וְהֵם חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה
which divides into five periods of two and a half years each.
כִּי יָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה י״ד) שֶׁחָמֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת בַּנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהֵם: נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה, חַיָּה, יְחִידָה
For as is known from Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 14), there are five levels to the soul: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah.
נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, וּנְשָׁמָה הִיא מַחֲשָׁבָה, דִּבּוּר, וּמַעֲשֶׂה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּכָל זֶה בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר בַּאֲרִיכוּת
Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah correspond to thought, speech, and action, as I have written at length elsewhere:
הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בַּכָּבֵד שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא דָּם, וְהַדָּם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ
action is centered in the liver, which is full of blood, and "the blood is the Nefesh";
וְהַדִּבּוּר בַּלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְדֹבֵר אֱמֶת בִּלְבָבוֹ", וְשָׁם מִשְׁכַּן רוּחַ חַיִּים כִּידוּעַ
speech resides in the heart, as written: "and speaks truth in his heart," where the spirit of life (Ruach) dwells, as is known,
וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם אֻנְקְלוֹס: "לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא", כִּי הַדִּבּוּר בָּרוּחַ
and Onkelos translated "a living soul" as "a speaking spirit," for speech operates through Ruach.
וְהַנְּשָׁמָה הִיא הַנֶּעְלֶמֶת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (דַּף ו׳ עַמּוּד א׳), וְהוּא הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ
And the Neshamah is the concealed level, as taught in the first chapter of Berakhot (6a), corresponding to thought in the brain;
שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁבַּלֵּב כְּבָר יֵשׁ בּוֹ גִּלּוּי, כִּי מְקוֹם הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב, וְהַהַרְגֵּשׁ הִיא הִתְגַּלּוּת
for what resides in the heart already has manifestation, since the heart is the seat of feeling, and feeling is revelation;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ הוּא נֶעְלָם וַעֲדַיִן לֹא קַיְימָא לִשְׁאֵלָה
whereas wisdom in the brain is concealed and not yet subject to inquiry,

אֶלָּא מִבִּינָה דְּאִיהִי לִבָּא, וְתַמָּן הַלֵּב מֵבִין, מִשָּׁם וָהֵילָךְ קַיְימָא לִשְׁאֵלָה, שֶׁכְּבָר הִיא בְּגִלּוּי לְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַמַּרְגִּישׁ, וְהוּא נִגְלֶה לַמַּרְגִּישׁ לָכֵן קַיְימָא לִשְׁאֵלָה
except through Binah (understanding) which is the heart, where the heart understands, from which point onward it becomes subject to inquiry because it is revealed to perception.
אֲבָל הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ הִיא הַנְּשָׁמָה שֶׁרוֹאָה וְאֵינָהּ נִרְאֵית, רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינָהּ מוּרְגֶּשֶׁת כְּלָל אַף בִּרְאִיַּת הַלֵּב, כְּעִנְיַן "וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה"
But wisdom in the brain is the Neshamah that sees yet is not seen, meaning it is not felt even through the heart's perception, as in "my heart saw much";
וְזֶהוּ "וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים", וְהָאַף בָּרֹאשׁ נִמְשָׁךְ מִן הַמּוֹחַ
and this is "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath (Neshamah) of life," where the nostrils in the head extend directly from the brain.
וְכָל אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה הֵם בֵּרוּרִים וּמַדְרֵגוֹת בְּעֶצֶם הָאָדָם, שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְיַגֵּעַ עַצְמוֹ לְתַקֵּן שְׁלֹשָׁה כֹּחוֹת אֵלּוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רַק לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
All these three internal levels belong to man's very self, requiring exertion to align them exclusively with the Will of Hashem.
אֲבָל שְׁנֵי הַכֹּחוֹת חַיָּה, יְחִידָה הֵם הַמַּקִּיפִים לָאָדָם
The two higher faculties, Chayah and Yechidah, however, represent the encompassing lights (Orot Makifim) around a person:
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם בִּפְנִימִיּוּת וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת כֹּחוֹתָיו שֶׁאֵין חֵפֶץ מַה שֶּׁזּוּלַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning that after perfecting his inner and outer faculties to desire nothing outside Hashem's Will,
צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁגַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁמַּקִּיף אוֹתוֹ, רָצָה לוֹמַר כָּל מַה שֶּׁחוּץ מִמֶּנּוּ וּמֵרְצוֹנוֹ, הַכֹּל הוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּלְבַד
he must know that all which encompasses him—everything outside himself and his own will—is solely the Will of Hashem alone;
וּמַרְגִּישׁ חַיִּים הַנִּצְחִיִּים בְּכָל מַקִּיפוֹ, בְּמַדְרֵגַת "כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִילִי" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין דַּף ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳)
feeling eternal life in all that surrounds him, on the level of "the entire world was created for my sake" (Sanhedrin 37a),
וְהוּא יַרְגִּישׁ בַּלֵּב חַיִּים הָאֲמִתִּיִּים בְּכָל הַמַּקִּיף אוֹתוֹ מֵעוֹלָם וּמְלוֹאוֹ
sensing true life in all that surrounds him throughout the entire universe,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקִּיף אוֹתִי אֶלָּא חַיֵּי עוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר נָטַע הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם מִכֹּחַ וְרָצוֹן הַשֵּׁם לְבַד
realizing that nothing surrounds him except the eternal life planted by Hashem through Divine Will alone.
וְהִנֵּה יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי מִינֵי הֶקֵּפִים לָאָדָם: לְבוּשׁ וּבַיִת, וְהַלְּבוּשׁ הוּא הַמַּקִּיף הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁסְּבִיב גּוּפוֹ
Man possesses two encompassing enclosures: clothing and a house, where clothing is the primary enclosure directly surrounding the body;
וְהִנֵּה כָּךְ יֵשׁ לְבוּשׁ לְכֹחוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם, וְהֵם כְּכָל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם, וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה לוֹ לְבוּשׁ שֶׁל חַיֵּי עַד
so too the faculties of the soul have worldly garments, and man must transform them into garments of eternal life:
הַיְנוּ שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁהוּא מְלֻבָּשׁ בּוֹ, בַּמֶּה שֶׁהַנֶּפֶשׁ מְלֻבֶּשֶׁת בְּכֹחוֹת מֵעִנְיְנֵי זֶה הָעוֹלָם, כֻּלּוֹ הַכֹּל הוּא רַק אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶה מַדְרֵגַת חַיָּה
that whatever enclothes the soul in worldly affairs is perceived purely as the Light of Hashem, which is the level of Chayah.
וְקִנְיַן בַּיִת רָצָה לוֹמַר מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ הַמַּקִּיפוֹ
And acquiring a house signifies a permanent, encompassing space,
כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל גְּמָרָא דִּבְכוֹרוֹת (דַּף ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "בְּנוֹ לָן בֵּיתָא בַּאֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא"
as I heard on the Gemara in Bekhorot (8b): "Build us a house in the airspace of the world,"
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת בַּיִת שֶׁל נַפְשׁוֹת הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי הוּא בַּאֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תְּפִיסָה בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר
for the true home of Jewish souls is in the free ether of the world, having no material grasping in physical space;
וְהַמָּקוֹם קָבוּעַ הוּא אֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא [שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוּם מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ כְּלָל, זֶהוּ קְבִיעוּתָם]
and this boundless ether [which is not physically fixed at all] constitutes their permanent dwelling.
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן "בֵּית עוֹלָמִים" שֶׁבֵּאַרְנוּ לְמַעְלָה, שֶׁמַּדְרֵגַת מִקְדָּשׁ הוּא הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר אוֹ הַכּוֹלֵל יַחַד כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים
This is the concept of the eternal Temple (Beit Olamim) explained above: the Sanctuary is the absolute unity encompassing all creatures together,
שֶׁהַכֹּל חוֹזֵר לִהְיוֹת אֶחָד, שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הַמַּקִּיף
where all returns to singular Oneness as the encompassing light;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא כְּעִנְיַן זֶה, אָז נִקְרָא "בֵּית מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ עוֹלָמִים"
and when this is achieved, it is called a "house, a place for Your eternal dwelling,"
כִּי הַמָּקוֹם קָבוּעַ לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא בְּעִנְיָן זֶה
for a permanent place for the House of Israel is possible only in this manner.
וְזֶהוּ מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה, שֶׁהוּא כָּל כָּךְ מַרְגִּישׁ אֲמִתּוּת הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר, עַד שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֶלָּא יְחִידָה בָּעוֹלָם
And this is the level of Yechidah, where one feels the absolute truth of Divine Unity so thoroughly that there exists only the Singular One in the universe;
וְהַדְּבָרִים אֲרֻכִּים, לֹא עֵת הֵאָסֵף בָּזֶה יוֹתֵר
and these matters are vast, and this is not the time to gather further upon this.
וְהִנֵּה לְבֵרוּר כָּל הַדְרָגָה שֶׁיּוּקְבַּע אֶצְלוֹ כְּעַמּוּד חָזָק
Behold, in order to clarify and integrate each spiritual level so that it becomes firmly established within a person like a steadfast pillar,
קָבְעוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּחֻלִּין (דַּף כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): "כָּל תַּלְמִיד שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה סִימָן יָפֶה בְּמִשְׁנָתוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׁנִים, שׁוּב אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה"
our Sages of blessed memory established, as recorded in Chullin (24a): "Any student who does not see a favorable sign in his study within three years will not see one thereafter";
כִּידוּעַ שֶׁבִּתְלָתָא זִמְנֵי הָוֵי חֲזָקָה, וְשָׁנָה הִיא הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם שֶׁל יָמִים
for as is known, three occurrences establish an enduring presumption (chazakah), and a full year represents a complete cycle of days.
וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה הָוֵי חֲזָקָה נַמֵּי לְאִידָךְ גִּיסָא, שֶׁאִם רוֹאֶה סִימָן יָפֶה הוּא מְבֹרָר לְטוֹב
And through three years an established presumption is likewise confirmed in the positive direction: if one sees a favorable sign, it is fully clarified and verified for the good.
וְיֵשׁ לְפָרֵשׁ עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה גַּם כֵּן שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל דִּלְעֵיל
In this same manner one may also explain the three years of debate between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel mentioned above;
וּלְכָךְ לְבֵרוּר כָּל מַדְרֵגָה עַל בֻּרְיָהּ צָרִיךְ שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים
therefore, for the thorough and definitive clarification of any spiritual level, three years are required.
וְיָדוּעַ בְּכָל מַדְרֵגוֹת זֶה אַחַר זֶה: סוֹף הָאֶחָד הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ רֵאשִׁית הַבָּא אַחֲרָיו
It is well known regarding all sequential spiritual ascents that the culmination of one level serves as the very inception of the one following it
[כְּעִנְיַן "מַה שֶּׁעָשְׂתָה חָכְמָה עֲטָרָה לְרֹאשָׁהּ, עָשְׂתָה עֲנָוָה עָקֵב לְסוּלְיָתָהּ" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א׳), וְכִידוּעַ מַאֲמַר חַכְמֵי הָאֱמֶת זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בָּזֶה]

[in the spirit of the dictum: "What Wisdom made a crown for her head, Humility made a heel for the sole of her foot" (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1), as is known from the masters of Kabbalah on this principle];
וּכְבָר מְבֹאָרִים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר כִּי "סוֹף" נִקְרָא לְעוֹלָם בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אַחַר הַמֶּחֱצָה
and it has already been explained elsewhere that in rabbinic terminology, a "terminus/end" is always defined once past the halfway mark,
כְּעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּקִדּוּשִׁין (דַּף י״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "כֵּיוָן דִּנְפַק מִפַּלְגָא, קָרוֹב לְאַלְפַּיִם קָרֵינַן לֵיהּ" [דְּרֻבָּא כְּכֻלָּא]

as our Sages stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin (12a): "Once it passes beyond the halfway mark, we already designate it as approaching two thousand" [for the majority is equivalent to the whole],
וְרֹאשׁ הוּא קֹדֶם הַמֶּחֱצָה, וּנְקֻדַּת הַחֲצִי הוּא הָאֶמְצַע הַחוֹלֵק בֵּין הָרֹאשׁ לַסּוֹף
whereas the "beginning" spans prior to the halfway mark, and the exact midpoint is the dividing axis that separates beginning from end.
לָכֵן דַּי לְכָל מַדְרֵגָה שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה
Therefore, for the internal integration of each distinct level, two and a half years are sufficient;
וּמֶחֱצָה הַשֵּׁנִי, שֶׁהוּא סוֹף מַדְרֵגָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתְחָלַת הַשְּׁנִיָּה
and the remaining final half-year, which terminates the first level, itself constitutes the inception of the second level.
וְגַם לְמַדְרֵגַת "יְחִידָה", שֶׁהוּא הָאַחֲרוֹנָה, דַּי שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה
And even for the level of Yechidah, which is the fifth and highest rung, two and a half years are sufficient;
כִּי הַגְּמָר וְהַסּוֹף זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם, רַק יִהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד, כַּאֲשֶׁר "בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח", "וְאֶת הַצְּפוֹנִי אַרְחִיק מֵעֲלֵיכֶם"

for the ultimate, absolute completion is beyond mortal human capacity in this world, being reserved solely for the Messianic Future when "He will swallow up death forever" and "I will remove the hidden corrupter/evil inclination far from you."
אָז יִהְיֶה גִּלּוּי הַיִּחוּד הָאֲמִתִּי, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה כְּלָל שׁוּם בְּחִירָה בְּיַד הָאָדָם עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִרְאֶה כְּאִלּוּ נִפְרָד, רַק יִחוּד בֶּאֱמֶת

Then the absolute, authentic Divine Unity will be fully revealed, wherein there will no longer be free choice in human hands that could make man appear distinct or separate, but only unveiled Oneness in truth;
אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אַף מִי שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לִקְצֵה מַדְרֵגַת "יְחִידָה", הוּא רַק לְמַדְרֵגַת שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה בָּהּ, שֶׁהוּא עַד הַתְחָלַת נְקֻדַּת הַסּוֹף שֶׁבַּמַּדְרֵגָה הַזּוֹ

however, in this world, even one who reaches the highest summit of Yechidah attains only up to the measure of two and a half years within it, reaching the very threshold of the culminating terminal point of that rung.
[וְיֵשׁ עוֹד דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ בְּעִנְיַן שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה, שֶׁהֵם שְׁלֹשִׁים חֳדָשִׁים
[There is also a deeper mystery in this period of two and a half years, which comprises exactly thirty months:
כִּי בֵּרוּר כָּל דָּבָר הוּא בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת (דַּף קי״א עַמּוּד ב׳): "עַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם מוֹקֵי אִינִישׁ אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ, טְפֵי לָא מוֹקֵי"

for the fundamental trial and clarification of any inner trait takes thirty days, as stated in Yevamot (111b): "Up to thirty days a person can restrain and hold himself, but beyond that he cannot maintain a false pretense";
דְּכַאֲשֶׁר כְּבָר עָבְרוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם מוֹקֵי אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ, הוּא מְבֹרָר שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעַ בְּעֹמֶק הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְכָךְ, וְכָךְ קִבַּלְתִּי בְּשֵׁם חָכָם אֶחָד
so that once thirty days have elapsed while maintaining that resolve, it is proven that the trait has permeated the deepest will of his heart, and so I received from a certain sage.
וְהִנֵּה יָדוּעַ "מְזֻקָּק שִׁבְעָתָיִם" — שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע
Now, it is known that the verse "refined sevenfold" refers to seven times seven,
כִּי הַזִּקּוּק הָאֲמִתִּי הוּא שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים, כְּמוֹ שִׁבְעָה נְקִיִּים לְטָהֳרַת נִדָּה וְזִקּוּקָהּ מִטֻּמְאָתָהּ
because true purification requires seven stages, as in the seven clean days required for the purification of a menstruant woman (niddah) from her impurity;
כִּי שֶׁבַע הִיא הֶקֵּף שָׁלֵם לְבִנְיַן הָעוֹלָם הַכְּלָלִי בְּשִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַבִּנְיָן, עַד שֶׁיָּצָא הַבִּנְיָן אֶל שְׁלֵמוּת הַנִּרְצָה
for seven represents the complete cycle for the cosmic structure across the seven days of Creation until existence reached its intended harmony,
וְכֵן לְבִנְיַן כָּל דָּבָר פְּרָטִי, שֶׁהַפְּרָט דּוֹמֶה לַכְּלָל
and likewise for the development of any specific entity, since every microcosm mirrors the macrocosm.
וּמָצִינוּ בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה "תִּסְפְּרוּ חֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם", וְאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג׳, דַּף צ״ז עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּעִנְיַן סְפִירַת הַנִּדָּה יָמִים נְקִיִּים מִטֻּמְאַת מִצְרַיִם

And we find regarding the Giving of the Torah: "You shall count fifty days," concerning which the Zohar states (Vol. III, 97a) that the Omer count functions like the counting of clean days to purify Israel from the defilement of Egypt;
וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע, כִּי "בַּעֲלִיל לָאָרֶץ" [לִישָׁנָא דְּגִלּוּי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (דַּף כ״א עַמּוּד ב׳)]
and this required seven times seven weeks, for in order to be "clear and evident to the earth" [a Talmudic expression denoting open revelation, as in Rosh Hashanah 21b],
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַזִּקּוּק נִגְלֶה, אָז צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְזֻקָּק שִׁבְעָתָיִם, שִׁבְעָה זִקּוּקִים דְּהוּא שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע, וְאָז זִקּוּק הַכֶּסֶף נִגְלֶה לַכֹּל
for the refinement to become outwardly manifest, it must be refined sevenfold—seven sets of purifications, which is seven times seven—whereupon the purity of the silver is evident to all;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּזִקּוּק אֶחָד, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים לְבַדּוֹ, אָז הוּא מְזֻקָּק אֲבָל אֵין גָּלוּי לְכָל רוֹאֶה עֲדַיִן
whereas in a single purification of seven alone, the substance is inwardly refined but its purity is not yet visible to every onlooker.
וְלָכֵן בְּעֵת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהָיָה הַגִּלּוּי הָאֲמִתִּי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עוֹד כְּמוֹתוֹ, הָיָה צָרִיךְ הַזִּקּוּק גַּם כֵּן לִהְיוֹת גָּלוּי לַכֹּל, וְלָכֵן צָרִיךְ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע
Therefore, at the Giving of the Torah, which was an unparalleled public revelation, the purification also had to be manifest to all, necessitating seven times seven;
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן שְׁמִטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת, וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ עוֹד
and this is likewise the inner mystery of the Sabbatical cycles and the Jubilee (Yovel); and this is not the place to elaborate further.
וְכֵן כָּאן: שֶׁיִּהְיֶה "בַּעֲלִיל לָאָרֶץ", צָרִיךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים פְּעָמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים, וְזֶהוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים חֳדָשִׁים
And so it is here: for the internal transformation to become openly established and manifest on earth, it requires thirty times thirty, which equals thirty months [two and a half years].
וְהִנֵּה בְּכָל הַחֲמֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת הֵם מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים חֳדָשִׁים
Thus, across all five soul levels, these total one hundred and fifty months,
וְהֵם מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים מִקְוֵה טָהֳרָה דְּיָם שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה, וְיִתְבָּאֵר לְקַמָּן עוֹד בְּעֶזְרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ]

which correspond to the one hundred and fifty measures of ritual purification (mikva'ot) in the molten Sea constructed by King Solomon, as will be further expounded below with the help of Hashem, Blessed be He].
וְהִנֵּה בְּכָל הָאַרְבַּע מַדְרֵגוֹת עֲדַיִן הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "נִבְרָא", שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא הִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת "יְחִידָה" שֶׁהִיא הַיִּחוּד הָאֲמִתִּי

Now, throughout the first four soul rungs, man still operates within the consciousness of being a separate "created being," having not yet reached the level of Yechidah, which embodies absolute Divine Unity,
מַדְרֵגָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל
which was the elevated stature of Rabbi Meir, as explained above.
וּבְאוֹתָם שְׁתַּיִם שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה שֶׁל מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה, שֶׁכְּבָר הִגִּיעוּ לְהַרְגָּשַׁת הַיִּחוּד הָאֲמִתִּי, שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת "שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא"
But during those two and a half years spent attaining Yechidah, when they reached the direct perception of true Unity—the vantage point of "not having been created"—
נֶחְלְקוּ מִמַּה הוּא הַנִּיחָא
they debated from which state true spiritual rest and satisfaction (neichah) is derived:
כִּי גַּם בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר יָדוּעַ שֶׁ"גַּם אִם רוּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁל [הָאֲמִתִּי] יַעֲלֶה עָלֶיךָ" לְמַעְלָה מִשִּׂכְלְךָ, שֶׁתַּרְגִּישׁ שֶׁאֵין לְךָ שׁוּם שֵׂכֶל מִשֶּׁלְּךָ כְּלוּם

for even at the summit of absolute Oneness, it is known that even "if the spirit of the true Sovereign rises over you" far above your mortal intellect, causing you to feel that you possess no independent intellect of your own,
עִם כָּל זֹאת "מְקוֹמְךָ [וּמַדְרֵגָתְךָ] אַל תַּנַּח", לָדַעַת גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת הַבְּחִירָה וְשֶׁיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם בְּיָדוֹ
nevertheless, "do not abandon your place," maintaining the conscious awareness of human free will and that the fear of Heaven rests squarely in man's hands.
וּ"מְקוֹמוֹ" רָצָה לוֹמַר: מַה שֶּׁהוּא נִבְרָא וּבְזֶה הָעוֹלָם אַל תַּנַּח, כִּי גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּיַחַד אֱמֶת גָּמוּר
"Your place" means: do not abandon your reality as a created being situated within this physical world, for both perspectives simultaneously constitute absolute truth.
וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְשֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם לַהֲבִינוֹ [וְהוּא קֻשְׁיַת הָרַמְבַּ״ם בְּעִנְיַן יְדִיעָה וּבְחִירָה וְתֵרוּצוֹ, עַיֵּן שָׁם בְּהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה] עַל בֻּרְיוֹ

And this paradox cannot be fully resolved by human intellect alone [which is the famous conundrum raised by Maimonides regarding Divine Foreknowledge versus Free Choice, and his resolution; see Hilchot Teshuvah ch. 5],
אִם לֹא מִי שֶׁהִשִּׂיג עִנְיַן מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה וְעִנְיַן הַיִּחוּדִים שֶׁזֶּהוּ יְסוֹדָן
except by one who has attained the level of Yechidah and the esoteric unifications (yichudim) that form their bedrock.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל בְּעִנְיַן "לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא", שֶׁיֵּדַע וְיָבִין הֵיטֵב שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת, שְׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מִתְיַחֲדוֹת יַחַד
And as explained above regarding the proclamation "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He," one must grasp with clarity that both perspectives are true and unify into one;
וְכָל זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם לַהֲבִינוֹ מֵעַצְמוֹ, אִם לֹא כְּשֶׁעֲזָרוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה בְּלֵב מֵבִין וּמַרְגִּישׁ
and mortal intellect cannot fathom this independently unless Hashem, Blessed be He, aids him to integrate it with an understanding, perceiving heart.
[וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל: "אֵיזֶהוּ בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא? זֶה הַסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאֻלָּה לִתְפִלָּה" (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ד׳ עַמּוּד ב׳)
[As I heard concerning the statement: "Who is a person destined for the World to Come? He who links redemption to prayer" (Berakhot 4b):
וְלֹא אָמַר: "כָּל הַסּוֹמֵךְ גְּאֻלָּה לִתְפִלָּה מֻבְטָח לוֹ" וְכוּלֵי, דֻּגְמַת "תְּהִלָּה לְדָוִד" דְּשָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא, יְעֻיַּן שָׁם

notice it does not say "Whoever links redemption to prayer is assured [a place in the World to Come]," as phrased regarding reciting Psalm 145 (Tehillah L'David) three times daily (Berakhot 4b, see there);
אֶלָּא שֶׁדָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם לִסְמֹךְ גְּאֻלָּה לִתְפִלָּה, שֶׁהוּא הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר [דִּבְטוּחוֹת וְיִרְאָה עַל פִּי דַּרְכּוֹ]
rather, linking redemption to prayer is not within human power alone, for it represents complete unification [fusing transcendent trust with reverent awe];
וְאֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם, רַק מִי שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עוֹלָם הַבָּא, הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ עַל זֶה]
it is beyond ordinary human reach, and only one who is inherently connected to the World to Come is granted divine assistance by the Holy One, Blessed be He, to achieve this].
וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁשְּׁתֵּי הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת מְיֻחָדוֹת אֶצְלוֹ בְּיִחוּד גָּמוּר, נֶחְלְקוּ מֵאֵיזֶה מֵהֶם הוּא הַנִּיחָא הַגְּמוּרָה

And since both spiritual levels were integrated within them in absolute unity, Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel debated from which dimension consummate satisfaction and spiritual rest (neichah) is derived.
דְּעַכְשָׁו שֶׁעֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ [שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, וְלֹא כָּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה], "יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ" וְכוּלֵי

Now, in our present reality where a person has not yet attained this supreme vantage [which was the rare level of Rabbi Meir, and not every person merits it], the Gemara advises: "Let him examine his deeds" (yefashpesh), etc.;
צָרִיךְ הַדִּקְדּוּק בַּמַּעֲשִׂים, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַגְדָּרוֹת וּגְבוּלִים: "אֶת זֶה תַּעֲשֶׂה" וְ"אֶת זֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה"
one requires painstaking scrutiny of actions, which consists of boundaries and halachic borders: "this you shall perform" and "this you shall not do";
שֶׁזֶּה מִצַּד הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהוּא בַּעֲלַת גְּבוּל וּכְמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ לְעֵיל
for this corresponds to the order of Creation, which is inherently finite, as we taught above.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן מִצַּד הַיִּחוּד הָאֲמִתִּי וּמַדְרֵגַת "עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא", אוֹמֵר עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר וּמַרְאֶה פָּנִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל

By contrast, from the perspective of absolute Divine Unity and the plane of "before the world was created," one is able to declare the impure pure and demonstrate its divine countenance, as noted above;
וְאֵין כָּאן גָּדֵר וּגְבוּל וּמִשְׁמוּשׁ בַּמַּעֲשִׂים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל
and there exist no rigid fences, boundaries, or scrutiny of deeds at that root, as was explained earlier.
וְעִנְיַן פְּלוּגְתָּא דִּ"יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ" וִ"ימַשְׁמֵשׁ" הִיא עַצְמָהּ הַפְּלוּגְתָּא בִּבְרָכוֹת (דַּף ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): אִי בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה גָּדוֹל אוֹ צַדִּיק גָּמוּר

And this debate between whether "he should examine his past deeds" (yefashpesh) or "scrutinize his present actions" (yemashmesh) is identical to the dispute in Berakhot (34b) regarding whether the penitent (Ba'al Teshuvah) or the fully righteous (Tzaddik Gamur) is greater:
"יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ" הוּא מַדְרֵגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה, שָׁב עַל הֶעָבָר
yefashpesh represents the level of the Ba'al Teshuvah, who searches and rectifies the past;
"וִימַשְׁמֵשׁ" בַּהֹוֶה — מַדְרֵגַת צַדִּיק גָּמוּר
while yemashmesh focuses on meticulously feeling and vetting the present—representing the level of the Tzaddik Gamur.
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר בֵּאַרְנוּם שֶׁהֵם שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת: יוֹסֵף וְדָוִד
And elsewhere we explained that these correspond to the two spiritual archetypes: Joseph and David

[תְּרֵין מְשִׁיחִין: יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, "הַגֶּבֶר הוּקַם עָל", וּכְדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה דַּף ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁהֵקִים עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, וְאֵין כָּאן מָקוֹם לְהַאֲרִיךְ]

[the two Messiahs: Joseph the Tzaddik, and King David, peace be upon him, "the man raised up on high," concerning whom our Sages stated (Avodah Zarah 5a) that he established the yoke of repentance; and this is not the place to elaborate further].
"יָם שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה" וְכוּלֵי (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ד עַמּוּד א׳)
"The molten Sea that King Solomon made" etc. (Eruvin 14a):
כְּבָר כָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם סוֹף הִלְכוֹת מִקְוָאוֹת רֶמֶז שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּמִּקְוֶה, עַיֵּן שָׁם
Maimonides already recorded at the conclusion of Hilchot Mikvaot the deep spiritual symbolism inherent in a ritual pool (mikveh), see there;
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שִׁלְהֵי יוֹמָא, לְהַמְשִׁיל טָהֳרַת עֲוֹנוֹת לִטְבִילַת הַמִּקְוֶה, יְעֻיַּן שָׁם
and this is likewise found in the teachings of our Sages of blessed memory at the conclusion of Yoma (85b), comparing the spiritual purification of iniquities to immersion in a mikveh, see there,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "דּוֹמֶה לְטוֹבֵל וְשֶׁרֶץ בְּיָדוֹ" וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם
where they stated: "he resembles one who immerses while holding a creeping creature (sheretz) in his hand," etc., see there
[דְּנָקְטֵי שֶׁרֶץ שֶׁהוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן מֵאֲבוֹת הַטֻּמְאָה בְּרֵישׁ כֵּלִים, וְהוּא שָׁכִיחַ]
[for they specifically selected a sheretz, which is the primary archetype of ritual impurity listed at the opening of Tractate Keilim and is widely prevalent];
וִיסוֹדוֹ בַּכָּתוּב: "וּמִכָּל גִּלּוּלֵיכֶם אֲטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם"
and the scriptural foundation for this is the verse: "And from all your abominations I will purify you."
וּתְשׁוּבָה, שֶׁשָּׁב לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל לִבּוֹ, רוֹמֵז לְמַיִם
Repentance (teshuvah), wherein one turns back to Hashem, Blessed be He, with one's entire heart, is alluded to by water;
וְרֶמֶז יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַחִנּוּךְ: כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בַּתְּחִלָּה מַיִם בְּמַיִם, וּכְאִלּוּ הַיּוֹם נוֹלָד וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּן שָׁם

and an allusion exists here as written in Sefer HaChinuch: just as the entire universe was originally water enveloped in water at the inception of Creation, so too the immersing penitent is as if reborn anew this day, see there.
וְעוֹד דְּבָרִים בְּגוֹ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל בִּדְבָרֵינוּ
There is an even deeper mystical reason here based on what was explained earlier in our words:
כִּי הַתִּקּוּן וַאֲמִירַת עַל טָמֵא טָהוֹר הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא", שֶׁהוּא הַיִּחוּד הַגָּמוּר, אָז הוּא תִּקּוּן הַקּוֹדֵם

for the ultimate spiritual rectification and the capacity to declare the impure pure operates at the transcendent level of "not having been created," which embodies absolute Divine Unity, where the primordial state of wholeness is restored.
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁמִּתְכַּסֶּה כֻּלּוֹ בַּמַּיִם, כְּאִלּוּ אֵינוֹ בָּעוֹלָם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
This state is actualized when one is completely submerged under water, nullified as though one did not exist as a separate entity in this physical world, as noted above;
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא דַּף פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): "מִי מְטַהֵר אֶתְכֶם? הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא"
and our Sages of blessed memory stated (Yoma 85b): "Who purifies you? The Holy One, Blessed be He."
הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וּמָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת הַשֵּׁם, כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים"
This mirrors the prophecy: "For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem, as the waters cover the sea."
וּכְשֶׁיִּטְבֹּל עַצְמוֹ בְּמַיִם אֵלּוּ, שֶׁהוּא דַּעַת אֶת הַשֵּׁם, וְיִתְכַּסֶּה כָּל גּוּפוֹ
When a person immerses himself completely in these waters—which represent divine consciousness (Da'at) of Hashem—submerging his entire body,
רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל כֹּחוֹתָיו יִהְיוּ שְׁקוּעִים בְּעֵסֶק זֶה, אָז נִטְהָר מֵעֲוֹנוֹת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ הַדְּבֵקוּת הַגָּמוּר
meaning that all his faculties and soul-powers become entirely absorbed in this holy occupation, he is purified of sins, for this constitutes total cleaving (devekut) unto the Divine;
וּבִלְבַד שֶׁכָּל גּוּפוֹ עוֹלֶה בָּהֶן
provided that "his entire body is covered by them [the waters] at once,"
שֶׁכָּל תַּאֲוֹתָיו וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו וְכֹחוֹתָיו בְּפִרְטֵי פְּרָטוֹת, אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם תְּשׁוּקָה וְרָצוֹן כָּל שֶׁהוּא לְעִנְיְנֵי זֶה הָעוֹלָם
meaning that all his desires, thoughts, and faculties in their finest details harbor no craving or will whatsoever for worldly vanities,
רַק לְמַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּשְׁקוּעִים בָּזֶה לְבַד, כֻּלָּם אֶחָד לֹא נֶעְדָּר
but strictly for that which fulfills the Will of Hashem, Blessed be He, all of them without exception being immersed in this alone.
וְשִׁעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים זֶה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, כִּי סְאָה הִיא הַמִּדָּה הַיּוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה מֵעֲבֵרוֹת
The Sages measured this required volume as forty se'ah, because a se'ah is the maximum biblical measure applied to sins and transgressions,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹטָה (דַּף ח׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "בִּסְאַסְּאָה" וְכוּלֵי, "אֵין לִי אֶלָּא סְאָה" וְכוּלֵי
as taught in Sotah (8b) on the verse: "B'sas'ah (in full measure)—I know only of a se'ah," etc.;
כִּי מְקוֹם הָעֲבֵרוֹת וְהַחֲטָאִים הוּא רַק בְּזֶה הָעוֹלָם
for the domain of transgressions and sins is confined exclusively to this physical world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב דִּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא יִשָּׁחֵט יֵצֶר הָרָע בְּשִׁלְהֵי סֻכָּה
as recorded at the end of Sukkah (52a), that in the Time to Come the evil inclination will be slaughtered;
וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק י״א): מִי שֶׁאֵין מְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת כָּאן, שָׁם מְשַׁמֵּר, עַד כָּאן
and in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11): "He who does not observe the Sabbath here [in this world] will observe it there [in Gehenna]," etc.;
וּבְפֶרֶק עוֹשִׂין פַּסִּין (עֵירוּבִין דַּף י״ט עַמּוּד א׳) דִּרְשָׁעִין אוֹמְרִין: "יָפֶה דַּנְתָּ" וְכוּלֵי
and in the chapter Osin Passin (Eruvin 19a), that the wicked confess: "You have judged well," etc.
וּלְכָךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּעַל גְּבוּל, כָּךְ הָעֲבֵרוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶם גְּבוּל
Therefore, just as this physical world is defined by finitude and limits, so too transgressions have a boundary;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן הַמִּצְוֹת אֵין לָהֶם גְּבוּל
whereas the commandments (mitzvot) are boundless and infinite;
וּלְכָךְ "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה בְּהַאי עָלְמָא לֵיכָּא" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב קִדּוּשִׁין דַּף ל״ט עַמּוּד ב׳)
and for this reason "there is no reward for a mitzvah in this world" (Kiddushin 39b),
דְּהַאי עָלְמָא בַּעַל גְּבוּל, וּשְׂכַר מִצְוָה אֵין לָהֶם גְּבוּל
because this physical world is finite, while the reward of a divine commandment is limitless.
וְאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּנִדָּה (דַּף ס״א עַמּוּד ב׳): מִצְוֹת אֵין בְּטֵלוֹת לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא
